# Archy Agents developer documentation

> Archy Agents is a multi-tenant platform for RAG, AI agents, multi-agent workflows and an MCP server. These docs explain how to integrate with and build on it.


<!-- source: index.md -->
# Archy Agents developer documentation

Archy Agents is a multi-tenant platform for building AI features on your own data and tools. It gives you:

- **Knowledge bases (RAG)**: upload or import documents, index them, and retrieve grounded context.
- **Agents**: configurable ReAct agents with a system prompt, a model, knowledge bases, skills and MCP tools.
- **Workflows**: coordinate several agents with sequential, parallel, routing, debate and composite (graph) workflows, including human approval checkpoints.
- **Bring-your-own LLM**: each organization connects its own provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint).
- **An MCP server**: platform capabilities as tools for Claude, Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT and your own agents.
- **A REST API** with an OpenAPI specification, bearer authentication and strict tenant isolation.

!!! tip "Start here"
    New to the platform? Follow [Run Archy locally](getting-started/local-setup.md), then the [Quickstart](getting-started/quickstart.md). You will have a working agent that answers from your documents.

## Choose your path

| I want to... | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand the model (tenants, projects, agents, workflows) | [Core concepts](getting-started/concepts.md) |
| Call the API from my backend or frontend | [Authentication and tokens](guides/authentication.md), then the [API reference](reference/index.md) |
| Create customers (organizations), projects and users from my own product | [Provisioning tenants and users](guides/provisioning.md) and the [tutorial](tutorials/provision-from-your-backend.md) |
| Connect an LLM provider | [LLM providers and models](guides/llm-providers.md) |
| Add documents and search them | [Knowledge bases](guides/knowledge-bases.md) |
| Build an assistant | [Agents](guides/agents.md) and the [support assistant tutorial](tutorials/support-assistant.md) |
| Orchestrate several agents | [Workflows](guides/workflows.md) and [Composite workflow graphs](guides/composite-workflows.md) |
| Use Archy from Claude, Copilot or Cursor | [MCP](mcp/index.md) |
| See how the system fits together | [Architecture](architecture/index.md) |
| Let an AI agent read these docs | [For AI agents](resources/for-ai-agents.md) |

## Base URLs

| Environment | API | MCP server |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted | `https://archy-agents.fly.dev` | `https://archy-mcp-server.fly.dev/mcp` |
| Local (docker compose) | `http://localhost:8000` | `http://localhost:8001/mcp` |

All API routes live under `/api/v1`. A running API serves Swagger UI at `/docs`. The specification that powers this site is published at [`openapi.json`](openapi.json).

## What is in these docs

- **Guides** explain each capability step by step with `curl` and Python examples.
- **Tutorials** combine several guides into an end-to-end build.
- **Architecture** has system, component, data model and sequence diagrams.
- **MCP** documents the tool catalog and how to connect clients.
- **API reference** lists every public endpoint with parameters, request bodies, examples and responses. It is generated from the code, so it matches the running service.

## Conventions used in the examples

Examples assume these environment variables. Each page repeats the ones it needs.

```bash
export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000   # or https://archy-agents.fly.dev
export ARCHY_TOKEN="<bearer token>"          # see Authentication and tokens
export ORG_ID="<organization id>"
export PROJECT_ID="<project id>"
```

Shell examples use [jq](https://jqlang.org) to pick values out of JSON responses. Python examples use [httpx](https://www.python-httpx.org) (`pip install httpx`).


<!-- source: getting-started/index.md -->
# Getting started

This section takes you from nothing to a working agent.

1. [Core concepts](concepts.md): the vocabulary and the tenant model. Ten minutes of reading that saves hours later.
2. [Run Archy locally](local-setup.md): start the API, database, vector store and MCP server with Docker Compose.
3. [Quickstart](quickstart.md): provision an organization, connect an LLM, add documents, create an agent and ask it a question.

## Integration patterns

Most teams use one of three patterns. They can be combined.

=== "Embedded in your product"

    Your backend owns customers and users. It uses a **service token** to create an organization, a project and users in Archy for each of your customers, pushes their LLM credentials, and then calls the API on their behalf (or lets their users call it).

    ```mermaid
    flowchart LR
        P[Your product backend] -- service token --> A[Archy Agents API]
        U[Your end users] --> P
        P -- user token --> A
    ```

    Read: [Provisioning tenants and users](../guides/provisioning.md), [Onboard customers from your backend](../tutorials/provision-from-your-backend.md).

=== "Direct API use"

    A developer or a service registers (or is invited), logs in, and calls the API with a user token. Good for internal tools and scripts.

    Read: [Authentication and tokens](../guides/authentication.md), [Quickstart](quickstart.md).

=== "Through MCP"

    AI clients (Claude, VS Code Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT or your own agent) connect to the Archy MCP server and use platform capabilities as tools: search a knowledge base, ask an agent, run a workflow.

    Read: [MCP overview](../mcp/index.md), [Connect a client](../mcp/connect-clients.md).


<!-- source: getting-started/concepts.md -->
# Core concepts

## The tenant model

Everything in Archy belongs to a tenant. Isolation is enforced on every query, so one customer can never read another customer's data.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    ORGANIZATION ||--o{ PROJECT : has
    ORGANIZATION ||--o{ LLM_CREDENTIAL : owns
    USER ||--o{ PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP : has
    PROJECT ||--o{ PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP : grants
    PROJECT ||--o{ AGENT : contains
    PROJECT ||--o{ KNOWLEDGE_BASE : contains
    PROJECT ||--o{ WORKFLOW : contains
    PROJECT ||--o{ MCP_SERVER : registers
    PROJECT ||--o{ SESSION : records
    PROJECT ||--o{ ARTIFACT : stores
    KNOWLEDGE_BASE ||--o{ DOCUMENT : indexes
    WORKFLOW ||--o{ WORKFLOW_VERSION : versions
    AGENT }o--o{ KNOWLEDGE_BASE : "grounded in"
    AGENT }o--o{ MCP_SERVER : "uses tools of"
    WORKFLOW }o--o{ AGENT : orchestrates
```

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Organization** (`org_id`) | A customer or company. Owns LLM credentials and org-wide defaults. |
| **Project** (`project_id`) | A workspace inside an organization. Most resources live in a project. |
| **User** | A person or service identity. A user can be a member of many organizations and projects and switches between them. |
| **Membership** | Links a user to a project with a role: `admin` or `permission-admin`. |

!!! note "Identifiers"
    All identifiers are UUIDs. Timestamps are ISO 8601 (UTC). Names are free text up to 255 characters.

Some resources can also be **organization-scoped** (agents, workflows, MCP servers and templates, connections). They are visible from every project in the organization and are addressed with `/orgs/{org_id}/...` routes instead of `/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/...`.

## Resources

| Resource | What it is | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **LLM credential** | A provider connection (API key, base URL) owned by an organization or a project. Encrypted at rest and never returned by the API. | [LLM providers](../guides/llm-providers.md) |
| **Model attachment** | A pin of `(credential, model)` to an agent, project or organization. Decides which model runs. | [LLM providers](../guides/llm-providers.md) |
| **Knowledge base** | A named collection of documents embedded into a vector store for retrieval. | [Knowledge bases](../guides/knowledge-bases.md) |
| **Agent** | A configured ReAct agent: system prompt, model, knowledge base, skills, tools, memory. | [Agents](../guides/agents.md) |
| **Workflow** | A definition that coordinates agents. Legacy types (`sequential`, `parallel`, `routing`, `debate`, ...) or `composite` graphs. | [Workflows](../guides/workflows.md) |
| **Session** | The persisted history of a conversation with an agent or a workflow run. | [Sessions](../guides/sessions-artifacts-usage.md) |
| **Run** | One execution of a workflow. Can be synchronous, streamed or asynchronous. | [Running and streaming](../guides/running-and-streaming.md) |
| **Artifact** | A file produced by a run or uploaded to a project. | [Sessions](../guides/sessions-artifacts-usage.md) |
| **MCP server** | An external Model Context Protocol server whose tools an agent can call. | [External MCP servers](../guides/mcp-servers-for-agents.md) |
| **Skill** | A packaged set of instructions an agent can use. | [External MCP servers](../guides/mcp-servers-for-agents.md) |

## Identities and tokens

Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. There are four kinds of token.

| Token | Obtained from | Acts as | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **User token** (JWT) | `POST /auth/login`, `/auth/register`, `/tenancy/switch` | One user in one org and project | Applications and scripts acting for a person |
| **Service token** (JWT, `token_type=service`) | Issued by the operator of the Archy deployment | A backend system with explicit scopes (`provision:org`, ...) | Provisioning tenants and users from your backend |
| **MCP API key** (`archy_mcp_...`) | `POST .../mcp-tokens` or OAuth | One project, scope `mcp:tools` (or `mcp:read` through OAuth) | IDEs and agent clients that use the MCP server |
| **External IdP token** (JWT via JWKS) | Your identity provider, when the deployment enables it | The user in the token claims | Single sign-on integrations |

See [Authentication and tokens](../guides/authentication.md) for details.

## Roles

A project membership has one of two roles.

- `admin`: manages the organization. Required for organization-level operations such as creating LLM credentials. Users created by [provisioning](../guides/provisioning.md) get this role.
- `permission-admin`: the role a user gets when they self-register with `POST /auth/register`. It can create and use agents, knowledge bases and workflows in its project, but it cannot manage organization-level LLM credentials.

!!! warning "Self-registered users cannot add LLM credentials"
    A user created with `POST /auth/register` owns a project but not organization admin rights. To add an LLM provider you need an `admin` membership. The fastest way to get one is the invite flow in [Provisioning](../guides/provisioning.md#bootstrap-an-organization-admin).

## How a request is resolved

1. The token is decoded and verified. Revoked or expired tokens return `401`.
2. The `org_id` and `project_id` in the path must match the token tenant. A mismatch returns `403`.
3. The route checks the role it needs (for example organization admin for LLM credentials).
4. Every database query is filtered by organization and project.

## Models and credentials

An agent runs on a model chosen by the [model resolution order](../guides/llm-providers.md#which-model-runs). In short: an attachment on the agent wins, then the project, then the organization, then the platform default. Only credentials that passed verification are used.

## Sync, streaming and async

| Mode | Use when | Endpoint style |
|---|---|---|
| Synchronous | A short request that returns a final answer | `POST .../query`, `POST .../execute` |
| Streaming | You want progress as it happens | Server-Sent Events (`.../stream`) or NDJSON |
| Asynchronous run | The caller cannot hold a connection (for example a serverless function) | `POST .../runs`, then poll `GET .../runs/{run_id}` |


<!-- source: getting-started/local-setup.md -->
# Run Archy locally

You can run the full platform on your machine in a few minutes. This is the recommended way to learn the API and to develop against it.

## What you need

- Docker with Compose v2
- `curl` and [`jq`](https://jqlang.org)
- Optional, for service tokens and the dev loop: Python 3.11 or 3.12 and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org)
- An API key for an LLM provider (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek or a local Ollama). You add it through the API later; nothing is baked into the stack.

## Start the stack

### 1. Create the credential encryption key

Archy encrypts every stored LLM provider API key with AES-256-GCM. The key is **required**: without it, creating an LLM credential fails. Generate a 32 byte base64 key once and keep it. If you lose it, stored credentials can no longer be decrypted.

```bash
export LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
```

The stock `docker-compose.yml` does not forward this variable, so add a `docker-compose.override.yml` next to it. Compose merges it automatically:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    environment:
      LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      # Only when you want to use a model server on your machine, for example Ollama.
      # SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS: "true"
```

### 2. Start the services

```bash
git clone <your archy-agents-scope repository url>
cd archy-agents-scope
docker compose up -d --build
```

Compose starts these services:

| Service | Port | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `api` | 8000 | The REST API. Runs database migrations on start. |
| `mcp-server` | 8001 | The Archy Platform MCP server (streamable HTTP). |
| `postgres` | 5453 | Metadata (organizations, projects, agents, workflows, sessions). |
| `qdrant` | 6333 | Vector store for knowledge bases. |
| `redis` | 6379 | Cache and queues. |
| `minio` | 9000, 9001 | S3-compatible object storage for uploaded documents. |

Check that the API is healthy:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/health
curl -s http://localhost:8000/health/readiness
```

Open the interactive API explorer at <http://localhost:8000/docs>.

!!! info "Defaults are for development only"
    The stack signs tokens with `JWT_SECRET_KEY=change-me`. Never use the default outside your machine. Set your own value in the environment before `docker compose up`.

## Create a service token

Provisioning endpoints need a **service token**. In production the operator of your deployment issues it. Locally you mint one with the same signing secret the API uses:

```bash
JWT_SECRET_KEY=change-me poetry run python scripts/generate_service_token.py \
  --subject my-backend \
  --scopes provision:org provision:project provision:user provision:user:read \
  --expires-in-minutes 120
```

Export the output:

```bash
export SERVICE_TOKEN="<printed token>"
export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
```

The command prints only the token. Service tokens carry scopes, not a tenant: the target organization is part of each request.

!!! note "Why a service token?"
    A self-registered user cannot manage organization-level settings such as LLM credentials, and only a service token can create organizations with chosen ids. The [Quickstart](quickstart.md) uses the service token once to create an organization and an admin, then continues with that admin's user token.

## The development loop

If you prefer to run the API on the host and only the dependencies in Docker:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres qdrant redis minio minio-init
cp .env.example .env.local        # local development loads .env.local
# add LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<base64 key> to .env.local
poetry install
poetry run alembic upgrade head
poetry run uvicorn src.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

`.env.local` points `DATABASE_URL` at `localhost:5433`. Compose publishes Postgres on `5453`. Update `DATABASE_URL` to the port you use.

Run the MCP server on the host:

```bash
export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
export ARCHY_MCP_TOKEN="<MCP API key>"      # see the MCP guide
poetry run python -m src.mcp_server
```

## Stop and reset

```bash
docker compose down          # stop, keep data
docker compose down -v       # stop and delete all data
```

## Configuration reference

The settings you are most likely to change. All are environment variables.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | local Postgres | SQLAlchemy URL of the metadata database |
| `QDRANT_URL` | `http://localhost:6333` | Vector store |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://localhost:6379/0` | Cache and queues |
| `S3_ENDPOINT_URL`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME` | MinIO in compose | Document storage |
| `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_ALGORITHM` | `change-me`, `HS256` | Signing of user and service tokens |
| `EXTERNAL_AUTH_ENABLED`, `EXTERNAL_AUTH_ISSUER`, `EXTERNAL_AUTH_AUDIENCE`, `EXTERNAL_AUTH_JWKS_URL` | off | Accept tokens from your identity provider |
| `SERVICE_TOKEN_BINDING_MODE` | `audit` | `enforce` requires service tokens to name the organizations they may act for |
| `LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | none, **required** | Base64 32 byte key that encrypts stored provider API keys. Optional rotation: `LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` and `LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID`. |
| `SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS` | `false` | Allow `http://` and loopback provider URLs. Local development only (for example Ollama). |
| `ALLOW_PLATFORM_LLM_FALLBACK_DEFAULT` | `true` | Whether an organization without credentials may use the platform default model |
| `PASSWORD_RESET_URL_BASE` | `http://localhost:3001/reset-password` | Base of the set-password links the invite endpoint returns |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | local origins | Allowed browser origins |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Log verbosity (logs are structured JSON) |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `connection refused` on port 8000 | The API container is still migrating. Wait for `docker compose ps` to show it healthy. |
| `401 Invalid token` on provisioning | The service token was signed with a different `JWT_SECRET_KEY` than the API uses. |
| `403 Missing scopes: provision:...` | Mint the token with the scope named in the message. |
| `500` when creating an LLM credential | `LLM_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not set on the API container. |
| Port already in use | Another process uses 8000, 5453, 6333 or 9000. Change the published port in `docker-compose.yml`. |

More in [Troubleshooting](../resources/troubleshooting.md).


<!-- source: getting-started/quickstart.md -->
# Quickstart

In this tutorial you create a complete tenant and a working agent that answers questions from your own document. You use the API only.

**You will:**

1. Provision an organization and a project.
2. Create an organization admin and log in.
3. Connect an LLM provider and choose the default models.
4. Create a knowledge base and add a document.
5. Create an agent grounded in the knowledge base and ask it a question.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[Service token] -->|1. provision| O[Organization and project]
    O -->|2. invite admin| A[Admin user token]
    A -->|3. credential and models| L[LLM provider]
    A -->|4. upload and index| K[Knowledge base]
    A -->|5. create| G[Agent]
    K --> G
    G -->|ask| R[Grounded answer]
```

**Before you start** you need a running API ([Run Archy locally](local-setup.md)), a `SERVICE_TOKEN` with scopes `provision:org provision:project provision:user`, and an OpenAI API key (any [supported provider](../guides/llm-providers.md) works; only the credential payload changes).

```bash
export ARCHY_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
export SERVICE_TOKEN="<service token>"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="<your provider key>"
```

## 1. Provision an organization and a project

Provisioning endpoints are idempotent upserts: you choose the ids, and repeating the call changes nothing.

```bash
export ORG_ID=$(uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')
export PROJECT_ID=$(uuidgen | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Acme"}'

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Support", "description": "Customer support assistant"}'
```

Each call returns `{"org_id": "...", "created": true}` (the project call also returns `project_id`).

## 2. Create an admin and log in

The invite endpoint creates the user, grants `admin` on the project, and returns a single-use set-password link. You use the token from the link to set a password, then log in.

```bash
export ADMIN_EMAIL="admin@acme.example"
export ADMIN_PASSWORD="a-long-unique-passphrase"

INVITE=$(curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/admins/invite" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\": \"$ADMIN_EMAIL\"}")

RESET_TOKEN=$(echo "$INVITE" | jq -r '.invite_link' | sed 's/.*token=//')

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"token\": \"$RESET_TOKEN\", \"new_password\": \"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}"

export ARCHY_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\": \"$ADMIN_EMAIL\", \"password\": \"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}" | jq -r '.access_token')
```

Confirm the token works:

```bash
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/whoami" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "subject": "9e0eb3c6-63d5-42db-98cd-f2ed378ca051",
  "org_id": "35af6d8d-f874-4b2b-9222-122092075307",
  "project_id": "117c77c5-5c13-49b1-aad7-9499442d967c"
}
```

From now on you use `ARCHY_TOKEN`. The service token is only for provisioning.

!!! tip "Why not just register?"
    `POST /auth/register` creates a user with its own organization in one call and is fine for experiments. That user has the `permission-admin` role and cannot create LLM credentials. See [Roles](concepts.md#roles).

## 3. Connect an LLM provider

Create the credential, then verify it. Verification makes a one token request to the provider. Only verified credentials are used at runtime.

```bash
CRED_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"provider\": \"openai\", \"display_name\": \"OpenAI\", \"api_key\": \"$OPENAI_API_KEY\", \"is_default\": true}" \
  | jq -r '.id')

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/$CRED_ID/verify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

A successful verification returns `{"success": true, "is_verified": true, "verified_at": "...", "latency_ms": 412, "error": null}`. A wrong key returns `success: false` with an `error` message and nothing is attached.

Now choose which models run by default. One attachment sets the chat model for the whole organization, and one sets the embedding model used by new knowledge bases:

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"gpt-4o-mini\"}"

curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"text-embedding-3-small\", \"dimensions\": 1536}"
```

!!! warning "Verify first"
    The model attachment call returns `422 Credential must be verified before attaching a model` if verification did not succeed. Fix the key first.

## 4. Create a knowledge base and add a document

```bash
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

export KB_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "handbook", "description": "Company handbook"}' | jq -r '.id')

cat > handbook.md <<'EOF'
# Acme handbook

Support hours are 08:00 to 18:00 CET, Monday to Friday.
Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.
Enterprise customers get a named contact and a four hour response target.
EOF

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/upload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -F "files=@handbook.md"
```

Upload stores the file and enqueues indexing. Check progress until `indexed_total` equals `files_total`:

```bash
curl -s "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
# {"files_total": 1, "indexed_total": 1, "indexing_total": 0}
```

Search it directly:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?", "top_k": 3}' | jq '.results[0].content'
```

## 5. Create an agent and ask it a question

```bash
export AGENT_ID=$(curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"name\": \"support-assistant\",
    \"description\": \"Answers support questions from the handbook\",
    \"config\": {
      \"sys_prompt\": \"You are a support assistant. Answer only from the knowledge base and say when you do not know.\",
      \"knowledge_base_id\": \"$KB_ID\",
      \"knowledge_base_top_k\": 4,
      \"temperature\": 0.2
    }
  }" | jq -r '.id')

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "What are your support hours and what is the refund window?"}'
```

The response contains the answer and the session id. Pass `session_id` on the next call to continue the conversation.

```json
{
  "agent_id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e",
  "session_id": "4e7c87f4-30d4-565f-a47b-9b4fca7f385a",
  "output": "Support hours are 08:00 to 18:00 CET, Monday to Friday. Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.",
  "meta": {}
}
```

You now have an organization, an admin, a connected model, an indexed knowledge base and a grounded agent.

## The same flow in Python

```python
import os
import time
import uuid
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

import httpx

BASE = os.environ.get("ARCHY_API_URL", "http://localhost:8000")
SERVICE = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SERVICE_TOKEN']}"}
PASSWORD = "a-long-unique-passphrase"

client = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=120)


def ok(response: httpx.Response) -> dict | list:
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()


# 1. Provision
org_id, project_id = str(uuid.uuid4()), str(uuid.uuid4())
ok(client.put(f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}", headers=SERVICE, json={"name": "Acme"}))
ok(client.put(
    f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}",
    headers=SERVICE,
    json={"name": "Support"},
))

# 2. Admin: invite, set password, log in
invite = ok(client.post(
    f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite",
    headers=SERVICE,
    json={"email": "admin@acme.example"},
))
reset_token = parse_qs(urlparse(invite["invite_link"]).query)["token"][0]
ok(client.post("/api/v1/auth/reset-password", json={"token": reset_token, "new_password": PASSWORD}))
login = ok(client.post("/api/v1/auth/login", json={"email": "admin@acme.example", "password": PASSWORD}))
user = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {login['access_token']}"}

# 3. LLM provider and default models
cred = ok(client.post(
    "/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials",
    headers=user,
    json={"provider": "openai", "display_name": "OpenAI", "api_key": os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], "is_default": True},
))
verified = ok(client.post(f"/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/{cred['id']}/verify", headers=user))
assert verified["success"], verified["error"]
ok(client.put(
    "/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org",
    headers=user,
    json={"credential_id": cred["id"], "model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"},
))
ok(client.put(
    "/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default",
    headers=user,
    json={"credential_id": cred["id"], "model_name": "text-embedding-3-small", "dimensions": 1536},
))

# 4. Knowledge base
scope = f"/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}"
kb = ok(client.post(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases", headers=user, json={"name": "handbook"}))
ok(client.post(
    f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb['id']}/documents/upload",
    headers=user,
    files=[("files", ("handbook.md", b"Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase.", "text/markdown"))],
))
while True:
    stats = ok(client.get(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb['id']}/stats", headers=user))
    if stats["indexed_total"] >= stats["files_total"] > 0:
        break
    time.sleep(2)

# 5. Agent
agent = ok(client.post(
    f"{scope}/agents",
    headers=user,
    json={
        "name": "support-assistant",
        "config": {"sys_prompt": "Answer only from the knowledge base.", "knowledge_base_id": kb["id"]},
    },
))
answer = ok(client.post(
    f"/api/v1/agents/{agent['id']}/query", headers=user, json={"message": "What is the refund window?"}
))
print(answer["output"])
```

- Understand how the model is chosen: [LLM providers and models](../guides/llm-providers.md).
- Stream the answer instead of waiting: [Running and streaming](../guides/running-and-streaming.md).
- Combine agents: [Workflows](../guides/workflows.md) and the [research pipeline tutorial](../tutorials/research-pipeline.md).
- Use the platform from an AI client: [MCP](../mcp/index.md).


<!-- source: architecture/index.md -->
# Architecture

These pages explain how Archy Agents is built, so that you can reason about performance, security and failure modes when you integrate.

- [System overview](system-overview.md): the system context, the deployable units and the data stores.
- [Components](components.md): the building blocks inside the API and the MCP server.
- [Flows](flows.md): sequence and state diagrams for the flows you will touch: provisioning, ingestion, agent queries, workflow runs, checkpoints and MCP authentication.

## Design principles

| Principle | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| **Tenant isolation first** | Every query is scoped by organization and project. A token for one tenant cannot read another tenant's data, even by guessing ids. |
| **Bring your own LLM** | Each organization owns its provider credentials. Archy does not use a shared key for your agents unless the operator enabled a platform fallback. |
| **Platform, not product** | The platform is domain neutral. Your product supplies the prompts, business rules and workflows; Archy supplies the runtime. |
| **Stateless MCP server** | The MCP server holds no database access. It calls the public API with the caller's token, so it can never do more than the API allows. |
| **Observable by default** | Runs persist their history, tool calls and token usage. Logs are structured JSON with request ids. |


<!-- source: architecture/system-overview.md -->
# System overview

## System context

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Clients
        APP[Your application or backend]
        CONSOLE[Web console]
        AI[AI clients: Claude, Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT]
    end

    subgraph Archy[Archy Agents]
        MCP[MCP server]
        API[REST API]
        WORKER[Indexing worker and schedulers]
    end

    subgraph Data[Data stores]
        PG[(PostgreSQL)]
        QD[(Qdrant)]
        RD[(Redis)]
        S3[(S3-compatible storage)]
    end

    subgraph External[External services]
        LLM[LLM providers]
        EMCP[External MCP servers]
        STO[Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox]
        ATL[Confluence and Jira]
        IDP[Identity provider via JWKS]
    end

    APP -->|HTTPS, bearer token| API
    CONSOLE -->|HTTPS, bearer token| API
    AI -->|MCP, OAuth or API key| MCP
    MCP -->|HTTPS, caller token| API
    API --> PG
    API --> QD
    API --> RD
    API --> S3
    WORKER --> PG
    WORKER --> QD
    WORKER --> S3
    API -->|chat and embeddings| LLM
    API -->|tool calls| EMCP
    API --> STO
    API --> ATL
    API -.->|verify tokens| IDP
```

## Deployable units

| Unit | Purpose | Scaling notes |
|---|---|---|
| **API** (`src.main:app`) | REST and WebSocket surface, authentication, agent and workflow execution, RAG | Stateless; scale horizontally. Runs database migrations on release. |
| **MCP server** (`python -m src.mcp_server`) | MCP tools over stdio or streamable HTTP | Stateless; one process per transport. Holds no database access. |
| **PostgreSQL** | Organizations, projects, users, agents, workflows, sessions, credentials (encrypted), audit | Source of truth for metadata. |
| **Qdrant** | Vector index per knowledge base | Rebuildable from documents by re-indexing. |
| **Redis** | Caching and queues | Loss is recoverable. |
| **Object storage** | Uploaded documents and artifacts | S3-compatible (S3, MinIO) or Azure Blob. |

## Trust boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Public
        C[Client]
    end
    subgraph Edge[Edge: TLS, rate limits]
        A[API]
    end
    subgraph Inner[Private network]
        D[(Databases and storage)]
    end
    subgraph Egress[Outbound with SSRF guard]
        E[LLM providers and tool servers]
    end
    C -->|bearer token| A
    A --> D
    A --> E
```

- **Inbound**: every route needs a bearer token except health probes and the OAuth discovery endpoints. Login and password reset are rate limited per client IP and per account.
- **Secrets**: provider API keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never returned. MCP server configuration secrets are write-only. Sensitive workflow inputs are masked in stored traces.
- **Outbound**: URLs that you configure (provider base URLs, MCP server URLs, document URLs) pass an SSRF validation that blocks private and loopback ranges unless the operator explicitly allows them.

## Environments

| | Local | Hosted |
|---|---|---|
| Start with | `docker compose up` | managed by the platform operator |
| API | `http://localhost:8000` | `https://archy-agents.fly.dev` |
| Service tokens | you mint them | issued by the operator |
| LLM credentials | yours | yours (per organization) |


<!-- source: architecture/components.md -->
# Components

## Inside the API

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Routes["HTTP and WebSocket routes (/api/v1)"]
        R1[auth, tenancy, integrations]
        R2[llm-providers]
        R3[rag]
        R4[agents, sessions, artifacts]
        R5[workflows]
        R6[mcp, mcp-tokens, skills]
        R7[realtime, voice]
    end

    subgraph Cross[Cross-cutting]
        AUTH[Principal resolution and token checks]
        TEN[Tenant context and guards]
        RL[Rate limits and request signing]
        OBS[Structured logging, request ids, audit]
    end

    subgraph Core[Core services]
        CRED[Credential and model resolver]
        AGENT[Agent runtime: ReAct, tools, memory, plans, hooks]
        RAG[RAG: readers, chunking, embeddings, indexing, retrieval]
        WF[Workflow engine: legacy executors and composite graph]
        MCPC[MCP client runtime and health scheduler]
        SESS[Sessions, run traces and artifacts]
        USE[Token usage metering]
    end

    subgraph Infra[Infrastructure adapters]
        DB[(PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy)]
        VEC[(Qdrant)]
        BLOB[(Object storage)]
        CACHE[(Redis)]
    end

    Routes --> Cross
    Cross --> Core
    AGENT --> CRED
    WF --> AGENT
    AGENT --> RAG
    AGENT --> MCPC
    AGENT --> SESS
    WF --> SESS
    AGENT --> USE
    Core --> Infra
```

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Routes** | Thin HTTP layer. They resolve the principal, validate the body and delegate to a service. |
| **Principal resolution** | Decodes user, service, external IdP and MCP API key tokens and rejects revoked ones. |
| **Tenant guards** | Ensure the organization and project in the path equal the token's tenant. |
| **Credential and model resolver** | Chooses `(provider, model, credential)` for each execution. See [model resolution](../guides/llm-providers.md#which-model-runs). |
| **Agent runtime** | Builds the agent from its stored config, registers tools (MCP servers, skills, knowledge base retrieval), manages memory and persists the session. |
| **RAG** | Reads PDF, Office, HTML, text, JSON and image files, chunks them, embeds with the knowledge base's model, indexes into Qdrant and retrieves with hybrid, vector or graph strategies. |
| **Workflow engine** | Executes legacy workflow types and composite graphs, supports checkpoints that pause for a human, versions every change and emits a unified run trace. |
| **MCP client runtime** | Connects agents to external MCP servers (HTTP, and stdio through organization templates), applies per-run tool allow-lists, and health-checks registered servers. |
| **Sessions and artifacts** | Persist conversation history, run traces, and files produced by runs. |
| **Usage metering** | Records token usage per call, aggregated by organization, project, model and time. |

## The MCP server

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CL[MCP client] -- "stdio or streamable HTTP" --> SRV[FastMCP server]
    SRV --> AUTHN[Bearer or API key check]
    AUTHN --> TOOLS[Tool modules: agents, kb, rag, workflows, ...]
    TOOLS -- "httpx, caller token" --> API[Archy REST API]
```

- It is a **client of the REST API**. There is no second implementation of any rule.
- The org and project for each call come from the caller's token, per request.
- You can restrict which tool modules a process exposes with `MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS`.

See [MCP](../mcp/index.md).

## Tenancy at the data layer

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T[Token: org_id, project_id] --> G{Path tenant equals token tenant?}
    G -- no --> F[403 Forbidden]
    G -- yes --> Q[Query with org_id AND project_id filters]
    Q --> D[(Database)]
```

Organization-scoped resources (agents, workflows, MCP servers, connections) use the organization filter alone and are visible in every project of that organization.


<!-- source: architecture/flows.md -->
# Flows

## Provision a tenant and bootstrap an admin

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant B as Your backend
    participant A as Archy API
    participant U as Admin user
    B->>A: PUT /integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id} (service token)
    A-->>B: org_id, created
    B->>A: PUT .../orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}
    A-->>B: project_id, created
    B->>A: POST .../orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite {email}
    A-->>B: invite_link (single use), user_id
    B->>U: Send the set-password link
    U->>A: POST /auth/reset-password {token, new_password}
    A-->>U: ok
    U->>A: POST /auth/login
    A-->>U: user token (org_id, project_id)
```

## Ingest and index documents

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant S as Object storage
    participant Q as Indexing job queue
    participant W as Indexer
    participant E as Embedding model
    participant V as Qdrant
    C->>A: POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents/upload (multipart)
    A->>S: store original file
    A->>Q: enqueue one job per document
    A-->>C: documents with status "uploaded"
    W->>Q: take job (running)
    W->>S: read file
    W->>W: extract text and chunk
    W->>E: embed chunks (organization credential)
    W->>V: upsert vectors
    W->>Q: succeeded (document status "indexed")
    C->>A: GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/stats
    A-->>C: files_total, indexed_total, indexing_total
```

An indexing job moves through the states below. A failed job keeps `error_type` and `error_message`; re-run it with `POST .../index`.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> queued
    queued --> running
    running --> succeeded
    running --> failed
    failed --> queued: re-enqueue
    succeeded --> [*]
```

## Ask an agent

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant R as Model resolver
    participant K as Knowledge base
    participant L as LLM provider
    participant T as MCP tools
    C->>A: POST /agents/{id}/query {message, session_id?}
    A->>A: authenticate, check tenant
    A->>R: resolve provider, model, credential
    R-->>A: verified credential or credential error
    A->>K: retrieve top_k chunks (if the agent has a knowledge base)
    loop until final answer or max iterations
        A->>L: messages, tools, context
        L-->>A: text or tool call
        opt tool call
            A->>T: call tool
            T-->>A: result
        end
    end
    A->>A: persist session, record token usage
    A-->>C: output, session_id
```

## Run a workflow asynchronously

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant W as Workflow engine
    C->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/runs {message, inputs}
    A-->>C: 202 run_id, status pending
    A->>W: start in background
    loop poll
        C->>A: GET .../runs/{run_id}
        A-->>C: status running
    end
    W-->>A: finished
    C->>A: GET .../runs/{run_id}
    A-->>C: status succeeded, output, audit
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending
    pending --> running
    running --> awaiting_input: checkpoint node
    awaiting_input --> running: resume with answer
    awaiting_input --> cancelled: cancel
    running --> succeeded
    running --> failed
    succeeded --> [*]
    failed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]
```

## Pause for a human and resume

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant H as Human
    C->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/execute
    A-->>C: status awaiting_input, pending_input, session_id
    C->>H: show the question
    H-->>C: answer
    C->>A: POST .../workflows/{id}/sessions/{session_id}/resume {answer}
    A-->>C: continues, status completed
```

## Connect an AI client to the MCP server

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as MCP client
    participant M as MCP server
    participant A as Archy API
    participant U as User (browser)
    C->>M: request without token
    M-->>C: 401 with resource_metadata
    C->>M: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
    M-->>C: authorization server = Archy API
    C->>A: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
    C->>A: POST /oauth/register (dynamic client registration)
    C->>U: open /oauth/authorize (PKCE S256)
    U->>A: sign in and approve
    A-->>C: authorization code on redirect URI
    C->>A: POST /oauth/token (code, code_verifier)
    A-->>C: access token
    C->>M: tools/call with Authorization: Bearer
    M->>A: same call with the caller token
    A-->>M: result scoped to the caller's tenant
    M-->>C: tool result
```

Clients that cannot run OAuth use an `archy_mcp_` API key instead. See [Connect a client](../mcp/connect-clients.md).

## Which model runs

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S([Execution starts]) --> A{Attachment on the agent?}
    A -- yes --> USE[Use that credential and model]
    A -- no --> B{Agent config pins credential_id and model_name?}
    B -- yes --> USE
    B -- no --> C{Project attachment?}
    C -- yes --> USE
    C -- no --> C2{Project platform default model?}
    C2 -- yes --> PLAT[Platform model, no credential]
    C2 -- no --> D{Organization attachment?}
    D -- yes --> USE
    D -- no --> D2{Organization platform default model?}
    D2 -- yes --> PLAT
    D2 -- no --> E{Agent config has a model_name?}
    E -- yes --> PLAT
    E -- no --> ERR[No model: error or echo mode]
```

A tier is skipped when its credential is missing or not verified. The platform tiers run only when the organization allows the platform fallback. When none applies the call fails with a `credential_error` rather than silently using a platform key.

# Guides

Step-by-step guides for each capability. Every guide has runnable `curl` and Python examples and links to the matching [API reference](../reference/index.md) pages.

| Guide | You learn how to |
|---|---|
| [Authentication and tokens](authentication.md) | Get and use user tokens, service tokens, MCP API keys and external tokens |
| [Provisioning tenants and users](provisioning.md) | Create organizations, projects, users and admins from your backend |
| [LLM providers and models](llm-providers.md) | Connect providers, verify credentials and choose which model runs |
| [Knowledge bases](knowledge-bases.md) | Ingest documents, index them and query them |
| [Agents](agents.md) | Configure agents and talk to them |

!!! tip "Recommended order for a new integration"
    Authentication → Provisioning → LLM providers → Knowledge bases → Agents → Running and streaming. Add workflows when one agent is not enough.


<!-- source: guides/authentication.md -->
# Authentication and tokens

Every API call needs a bearer token, except the health probes, the `/auth/*` endpoints (register, login, forgot and reset password) and the OAuth endpoints:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

A missing or malformed header returns `401` with `{"detail": "Missing bearer token"}`.

## Token types at a glance

| Token | Identifies | Lifetime | Where it is accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| User token (JWT) | A user acting in one org and project | Login: 8 hours, or 7 days with `remember_me`. Register and tenant switch: 30 minutes. | All tenant routes |
| Service token (JWT) | A backend system and its scopes | Chosen by the issuer | Provisioning routes, and tenant routes for the organization and project in the request |
| MCP API key (`archy_mcp_...`) | A project and a scope (`mcp:tools`; `mcp:read` when granted through OAuth) | 1 to 365 days, or never | MCP server and the MCP routes of the API |
| External IdP token (JWT) | The user named in the claims | Set by your IdP | All tenant routes, when the operator enabled it |

## User tokens

### Register

Creates a user together with a new organization and project, and returns a token.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/register" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "dev@example.com", "password": "a-long-unique-passphrase", "org_name": "Acme", "project_name": "Support"}'
```

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "user_id": "0888cd4e-1746-4009-ad52-53f369120227",
  "org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "available_orgs": [{"org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865", "name": "Acme", "project_count": 1}]
}
```

- `email` must be unique; a duplicate returns `409`.
- `password` is 8 to 128 characters (a shorter one fails request validation with `422`).
- The returned token lasts **30 minutes**. Use `POST /auth/login` (8 hours, or 7 days with `remember_me`) for longer sessions.
- A self-registered user has the `permission-admin` role. See [Roles](../getting-started/concepts.md#roles).

### Log in

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "dev@example.com", "password": "a-long-unique-passphrase", "remember_me": false}'
```

The response has the same shape as register. Wrong credentials return `401 Invalid credentials` for every cause (unknown email, wrong password, inactive account), so the response does not reveal which accounts exist.

### Inspect and switch tenant

A user can belong to several organizations and projects. The token is bound to one pair; switch to get a new token for another pair.

```bash
# Who am I, and in which tenant?
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/whoami" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Organizations and projects I belong to
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/orgs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/projects?org_id=$ORG_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Switch; the response contains a new access_token
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/tenancy/switch" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG_ID\", \"project_id\": \"$PROJECT_ID\"}"
```

Switching to a project you are not a member of returns `403 Not a member of this project`. The new token lasts 30 minutes, and the switched organization and project become your default for the next login.

### Reset a password

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/forgot-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email": "dev@example.com"}'

curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"token": "<token from the email link>", "new_password": "a-new-long-unique-passphrase"}'
```

`forgot-password` always returns `200`, whether or not the email exists. Reset tokens are single use and expire. A successful reset invalidates every token issued earlier for that user.

### Python helper

```python
import os
import httpx


class ArchyClient:
    """Logs in, injects the bearer token and logs in again once on a 401."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, email: str, password: str) -> None:
        self.http = httpx.Client(base_url=base_url, timeout=60)
        self.email, self.password = email, password
        self.login()

    def login(self) -> None:
        r = self.http.post("/api/v1/auth/login", json={"email": self.email, "password": self.password})
        r.raise_for_status()
        body = r.json()
        self.org_id, self.project_id = body["org_id"], body["project_id"]
        self.http.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {body['access_token']}"

    def request(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs) -> httpx.Response:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code == 401:
            self.login()
            response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response


client = ArchyClient(os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"], os.environ["ARCHY_EMAIL"], os.environ["ARCHY_PASSWORD"])
print(client.request("GET", "/api/v1/tenancy/whoami").json())
```

### Rate limits

Register and login are throttled per client IP and per account; reset-password per client IP and per reset token. When the budget is used up the API returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header (the length of the throttle window in seconds, 60 by default). Back off for at least that long. `forgot-password` is throttled silently: it keeps returning `200`.

## Service tokens

A service token authenticates a **system**, not a person. It normally carries scopes and no tenant. You use it to provision organizations, projects and users.

Claims of a service token:

| Claim | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sub` | Name of the calling system |
| `token_type` | `service` |
| `scope` | Space separated scopes |
| `org_ids` | Optional list of organization ids the token may act for |
| `exp` | Expiry |

Scopes:

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `provision:org` | `PUT /integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}` |
| `provision:project` | `PUT .../orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}` |
| `provision:user` | `PUT .../users/{user_id}` and `POST .../orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite` |
| `provision:user:read` | `GET .../users/by-email/{email}` |
| `provision:credential` | Push and delete LLM credentials for an organization |
| `tenant:act` | Needed together with `org_ids` when the deployment runs in `enforce` binding mode |

!!! info "Tenant binding"
    A deployment can run service tokens in `audit` mode (default: every use is logged with the organization it targeted) or `enforce` mode (on routes that target an organization the token must have `tenant:act` and list the organization in `org_ids`, otherwise `403 Forbidden`). The user lookup by email is only audited. Ask the operator which mode applies and request a token bound to the organizations you manage.

Service tokens are issued by the operator of the deployment. For local development you can mint one yourself, see [Run Archy locally](../getting-started/local-setup.md#create-a-service-token).

Using a service token on a route that needs a user returns `403 User token required`; using a user token on a provisioning route returns `403 Service token required`.

### Acting on tenant routes

A service token with at least one scope can also call the tenant routes (agents, knowledge bases, workflows, runs, ...) for the organization and project named in the **path**. This is how a backend operates a customer's workspace without holding a user session. Rules to know:

- The tenant comes from the request: the `org_id` and `project_id` in the path (`/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/...`) or, on routes that take them as optional query parameters (for example `/agents/{agent_id}/query`), from `?org_id=...&project_id=...`. Organization-scoped routes need only `org_id`. Without a tenant the API returns `401 Missing org_id`, which is why `GET /tenancy/whoami` returns `401` for a service token.
- It has **no organization admin rights**. Operations that need an `admin` user, such as `POST /llm-providers/credentials?org_id=...&project_id=...` or `PUT /llm-providers/model-attachments/org?org_id=...`, return `403 Org admin role required`. Push credentials with the provisioning endpoint and pin a model in the agent config instead (see [Onboard customers from your backend](../tutorials/provision-from-your-backend.md)).
- In `enforce` binding mode the token must carry the `tenant:act` scope and list the organization in `org_ids`, otherwise the API returns `403 Forbidden`.
- A run started this way has no initiating user, so personal connections are unavailable to it.

## MCP API keys

An API key lets an IDE or agent client use the MCP server without an interactive login.

```bash
# Create (a user token, or a service token for that organization and project). The raw token is shown once.
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "my-ide", "expires_in_days": 90}'

# List, revoke (stops working, row kept) or delete with DELETE .../mcp-tokens/$TOKEN_ID
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/mcp-tokens/$TOKEN_ID/revoke" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "id": "0dd516ed-3c38-47a7-bfd1-3dd7cec3be3f",
  "name": "my-ide",
  "token_prefix": "archy_mcp_0a1b2c3d",
  "token": "archy_mcp_0a1b2c3d<random characters, shown once>",
  "expires_at": "2027-02-15T09:09:03.996701",
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:03.997580"
}
```

`expires_in_days` is 1 to 365 and defaults to **90** when omitted; send `null` explicitly for a key that never expires. The response (`201`) also contains `org_id`, `project_id` and `description`. Store the `token` value in a secret manager immediately. It cannot be read again. See [Connect a client](../mcp/connect-clients.md) for scopes and usage.

## External identity provider tokens

If you operate your own deployment you can let Archy trust tokens from your IdP (Microsoft Entra, Auth0, Keycloak or any OIDC provider that publishes a JWKS):

```bash
EXTERNAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true
EXTERNAL_AUTH_ISSUER=https://login.example.com/
EXTERNAL_AUTH_AUDIENCE=archy-api
EXTERNAL_AUTH_JWKS_URL=https://login.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
EXTERNAL_AUTH_ALGORITHMS=RS256
```

The token must carry `iss`, `aud` and a subject (`sub`, or `oid`, `appid`, `azp` or `client_id`). A **user** token must also carry `org_id` and `project_id` claims, otherwise it is rejected. Application-only tokens (`token_type=service`, `grant_type=client_credentials`, `idtyp=app`, or `roles` without `scp` or `scope`) are treated as service tokens. Scopes come from the `scope` claim; if it is absent, from `scp`; if that is absent, from `roles`. The role `org-admin` grants organization admin rights. The deployment refuses external tokens when issuer and audience are not configured.

## Revocation and security notes

- **Password reset revokes tokens.** Tokens issued by Archy carry a version. Resetting the password increments it, so older tokens return `401 Token revoked`.
- **Deactivated users stop working.** A deactivated user's Archy tokens and MCP keys are rejected. External IdP tokens and service tokens are not revoked this way: they stay valid until they expire, so revoke them at the source.
- **Tenant mismatch is `403`.** If the `org_id` or `project_id` in the path differ from the token, the API returns `403 Forbidden` without saying whether the resource exists.
- **Keep tokens out of logs and URLs.** Send them only in the `Authorization` header and never log them in your own code.
- **Use the narrowest token.** Keys created with the API carry the write-capable `mcp:tools` scope; for read-only clients let the client request `mcp:read` through OAuth. Bind service tokens to organizations in `enforce` mode.


<!-- source: guides/provisioning.md -->
# Provisioning tenants and users

If you embed Archy in your own product, your backend creates the tenants. Provisioning endpoints let a **service token** create organizations, projects and users with ids that you choose, so your customer records and Archy tenants map one to one.

!!! info "You need"
    A service token with the scopes you use (see [Authentication](authentication.md#service-tokens)). All provisioning calls are idempotent upserts: calling them again with the same ids is safe, which makes them easy to retry from an outbox or a job queue.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CUST[Your customer record] -->|deterministic UUID| ORG[Organization]
    CUST -->|per workspace| PRJ[Project]
    CUST -->|per user| USR[User and membership]
    ORG --> PRJ
    PRJ --> USR
```

## Choose your ids

Archy accepts any UUID. Derive them deterministically from your own ids so that you never have to store a mapping and a retry is always the same call:

```python
import uuid

ARCHY_NAMESPACE = uuid.UUID("6f1c2f66-8f5b-4c60-9a32-0d8f0a1a2b3c")  # pick one and keep it forever


def archy_id(kind: str, your_id: str) -> str:
    return str(uuid.uuid5(ARCHY_NAMESPACE, f"{kind}:{your_id}"))


org_id = archy_id("org", "customer-1042")
project_id = archy_id("project", "customer-1042/default")
user_id = archy_id("user", "user-77")
```

## Create an organization

`PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}` · scope `provision:org`

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Globex", "settings": {"plan": "team"}}'
```

```json
{"org_id": "084d6557-5155-4851-88e3-192bea708c64", "created": true}
```

`settings` is a free-form object stored on the organization. Calling again updates `name`, **replaces** `settings` as a whole (omitting it clears it) and returns `created: false`.

!!! warning "Settings also hold platform keys"
    Archy stores the organization's embedding default, platform default model and the `allow_platform_llm_fallback` flag in the same `settings` object. A later upsert that does not send them removes them. Keep your own keys in `settings` and read the current value (or re-apply those defaults) before you re-provision an organization that already has LLM settings.

## Create a project

`PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}` · scope `provision:project`

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "Helpdesk", "description": "Support workspace"}'
```

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Created or updated |
| `404` | The organization does not exist. Create it first. |
| `409` with `project_org_conflict` | The project id already exists under another organization. Archy never moves a project between organizations. |

## Create a user

`PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/{user_id}` · scope `provision:user`

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/$USER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\": \"ada@globex.example\", \"org_id\": \"$ORG_ID\", \"project_id\": \"$PROJECT_ID\"}"
```

```json
{
  "user_id": "3a2f6241-68c1-441a-bc51-fafa36ac9fda",
  "org_id": "084d6557-5155-4851-88e3-192bea708c64",
  "project_id": "5348cb7c-a373-498c-9daf-bf74e24abbb8",
  "created": true
}
```

What this call does:

- Creates the user if the id is new, with a random unusable password. Your system, or the [invite flow](#bootstrap-an-organization-admin), is the source of truth for how this user signs in.
- Adds a membership with the `admin` role on the project. A user can be provisioned into many projects and organizations by calling again.
- For an existing user it only adds the membership. It never changes the email, the password, `is_active` or the user's active tenant.

Conflicts return `409` with a machine readable `detail.code`:

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `email_in_use` | Another user already owns this email |
| `email_mismatch` | The user id exists with a different email; emails never change |
| `concurrent_update` | Two writers raced; retry |

If the `user_id` already belongs to another user, the call fails with `email_mismatch` (or `email_in_use`).

## Bootstrap an organization admin

`POST /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite` · scope `provision:user`

Creates (or finds) a human admin by email, grants access to projects, and returns a **single-use set-password link** you can send in your own onboarding email.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/admins/invite" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "boss@globex.example"}'
```

```json
{
  "user_id": "71130610-41da-45f8-a058-9c4ba739a71d",
  "org_id": "084d6557-5155-4851-88e3-192bea708c64",
  "project_ids": ["5348cb7c-a373-498c-9daf-bf74e24abbb8"],
  "created_user": true,
  "existing_user": false,
  "existing_org_ids": [],
  "invite_link": "https://app.example.com/reset-password?token=Fg3UMgFDs8J-25ic0K3gBsEK_9H_sw83XSpfgfqx10Y",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-17T10:09:04.679975Z"
}
```

| Request field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | Required. Matched case-insensitively. |
| `user_id` | Optional id to use when the user is created. If it already belongs to another user the call fails with `409 user_id_in_use`. |
| `project_ids` | Projects to grant. Omit to grant all current projects of the organization. |
| `role` | `admin` (default) or `permission-admin`. A re-invite changes a role only when you pass one. |
| `is_active` | Applied only when the user is created. |

Notes:

- The organization must already have at least one project (`400` otherwise).
- For an **existing** user (same email) no link is issued: `invite_link` and `expires_at` are `null`, `existing_user` is `true`, and only memberships are added. `existing_org_ids` is internal information; do not show it to tenant users.
- The link base is the deployment setting `PASSWORD_RESET_URL_BASE`. The link carries a `token` query parameter. Your onboarding page posts it to `POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password` with the new password, and the user can then log in.

To finish the bootstrap without a browser (scripts, tests, CI):

```bash
TOKEN=$(echo "$INVITE" | jq -r '.invite_link' | sed 's/.*token=//')
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"token\": \"$TOKEN\", \"new_password\": \"a-long-unique-passphrase\"}"
```

## Look up a user by email

`GET /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/by-email/{email}` · scope `provision:user:read`

```bash
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/users/by-email/ada@globex.example" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN"
```

Returns the user id and active tenant, or `404`. Several accounts that differ only by case give `409 email_ambiguous`.

## Push LLM credentials (optional)

If your product stores the customer's provider keys, you can push them instead of asking the customer to call the LLM endpoints. Scope `provision:credential`.

`PUT /api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/llm-credentials`

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/$ORG_ID/llm-credentials" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "credentials": [{
      "credential_id": "5e1f3c52-2f67-4b5e-9d51-0c2f7f3e8a10",
      "provider": "openai",
      "display_name": "Customer OpenAI",
      "api_key": "<provider key>",
      "is_default": true
    }]
  }'
```

```json
{"org_id": "...", "upserted": 1, "created": 1, "updated": 0}
```

- Items are upserted by `credential_id`, which you supply, so retries are safe.
- A credential can be scoped to a project with `project_id`.
- `DELETE .../llm-credentials/{credential_id}` is idempotent: deleting an absent credential returns `deleted: false`, not `404`. A credential owned by another organization is never deleted (`409`).
- Every push **sets** `is_verified`, `verified_at` and `is_default` to the values you send (all default to `false`). Send `is_verified: true` on every push if you verified the key yourself; a later push without it un-verifies a credential, and unverified credentials are skipped at runtime. To verify through Archy instead, an admin user calls `POST /llm-providers/credentials/{id}/verify`.
- `project_id` is fixed when a credential is first created; later pushes do not move it.

### Signed requests

A deployment can require signed requests on this channel (`PROVISIONING_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`). The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical string, sent in three headers:

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time


def signed_headers(secret: str, method: str, path: str, body: bytes) -> dict[str, str]:
    timestamp = str(int(time.time()))
    nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
    signing_string = "\n".join([method.upper(), path, timestamp, nonce, hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()])
    signature = hmac.new(secret.encode(), signing_string.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return {"X-Archy-Timestamp": timestamp, "X-Archy-Nonce": nonce, "X-Archy-Signature": signature}
```

`path` is the request path without query string. The timestamp must be within the configured window (300 seconds by default) and every nonce is accepted once. A failed check returns `401 Invalid request signature`.

## How your users sign in

The provisioned user exists; now they need a token. Pick one:

| Approach | How | Choose when |
|---|---|---|
| **Set-password link** | Send the `invite_link`; the user sets a password and logs in with `POST /auth/login` | You want Archy to own the credentials |
| **Your identity provider** | The operator enables external auth; your IdP issues tokens with `org_id` and `project_id` claims | You already run SSO |
| **Your backend as proxy** | Your backend holds a user token (for example from a service account user) and calls Archy for your users | The end user never talks to Archy directly |

## A provisioning client in Python

```python
import os
import httpx


class Provisioner:
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, service_token: str) -> None:
        self.http = httpx.Client(
            base_url=base_url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {service_token}"}, timeout=30
        )

    def _send(self, method: str, url: str, **kwargs) -> dict:
        response = self.http.request(method, url, **kwargs)
        if response.status_code == 409:
            raise RuntimeError(response.json()["detail"])  # {"code": ..., "message": ...}
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()

    def ensure_org(self, org_id: str, name: str) -> dict:
        return self._send("PUT", f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}", json={"name": name})

    def ensure_project(self, org_id: str, project_id: str, name: str) -> dict:
        return self._send(
            "PUT",
            f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}",
            json={"name": name},
        )

    def invite_admin(self, org_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
        return self._send(
            "POST", f"/api/v1/integrations/provisioning/orgs/{org_id}/admins/invite", json={"email": email}
        )


p = Provisioner(os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"], os.environ["SERVICE_TOKEN"])
# archy_id is the helper from "Choose your ids"
org, project = archy_id("org", "customer-1042"), archy_id("project", "customer-1042/default")
p.ensure_org(org, "Globex")
p.ensure_project(org, project, "Helpdesk")
print(p.invite_admin(org, "boss@globex.example")["invite_link"])
```

## Error reference

| Status | Typical cause |
|---|---|
| `400` | Inviting an admin into an organization without projects |
| `401` | Invalid token or invalid request signature |
| `403 Missing scopes: ...` | Mint the token with the named scope |
| `403 Service token required` | A user token was used on a provisioning route |
| `403 Forbidden` | `enforce` binding mode and the token lacks `tenant:act` or does not list the organization in `org_ids` (`PUT .../users/{id}` checks the organization in the request body) |
| `404` | Organization or project not found |
| `409` | See the codes above |

Continue with [LLM providers and models](llm-providers.md).


<!-- source: guides/llm-providers.md -->
# LLM providers and models

Archy uses a **bring-your-own-LLM** model: every organization connects its own provider and chooses which model each agent runs on. Provider API keys are encrypted at rest and are never returned by any endpoint.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CRED[LLM credential<br/>provider, base URL, API key] -->|verify| OK[Verified]
    OK --> ATT[Model attachment<br/>credential + model name]
    ATT --> A1[Agent]
    ATT --> A2[Project default]
    ATT --> A3[Organization default]
    OK --> EMB[Embedding default<br/>for knowledge bases]
```

## Supported providers

`GET /api/v1/llm-providers/presets` returns the catalog (no secrets). A preset maps a friendly choice to a backend provider type plus defaults.

| Preset `key` | `provider` to send | Default `base_url` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `azure_openai` | `azure_openai` | your resource endpoint (required) | Also needs `api_version` (default `2024-12-01-preview`). The model name is the **deployment name**. |
| `openai` | `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | |
| `groq` | `openai_compatible` | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | |
| `deepseek` | `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | Chat only; no embeddings. |
| `gemini` | `openai_compatible` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | |
| `claude` | `openai_compatible` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` | |
| `cloudflare` | `openai_compatible` | none; the preset returns `base_url_template` `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/v1` | Replace `{account_id}` and send the result as `base_url`. |
| `ollama` | `ollama` | `http://localhost:11434` | Local models. The operator must allow local URLs. |
| `custom` | `openai_compatible` | none (required) | Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. |

Providers whose models can be listed (`supports_model_list` is `true` in the presets) are `openai`, `deepseek`, `ollama` and every `openai_compatible` preset. `azure_openai` cannot list deployments.

## Add a credential

Changing LLM configuration needs an **admin**: creating, updating, deleting, setting a default and verifying credentials, and also model attachments, the platform default model and the embedding default. You are an admin when you have the `admin` role on the project in your token, the `org-admin` role from your identity provider, or a platform admin grant. Reads (list, get, models, presets, `test`) need only membership. See [Roles](../getting-started/concepts.md#roles).

The credential belongs to the organization of your token. Set `project_id` to scope it to one project.

=== "OpenAI"

    ```bash
    curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"provider": "openai", "display_name": "OpenAI production", "api_key": "<key>"}'
    ```

=== "Azure OpenAI"

    ```bash
    curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "provider": "azure_openai",
        "display_name": "Azure EU",
        "api_key": "<key>",
        "base_url": "https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/",
        "api_version": "2024-12-01-preview",
        "extra_config": {"test_model": "<your deployment name>"}
      }'
    ```

=== "Anthropic Claude"

    ```bash
    curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "provider": "openai_compatible",
        "display_name": "Claude",
        "api_key": "<key>",
        "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1",
        "extra_config": {"test_model": "<a Claude model id>"}
      }'
    ```

=== "Ollama (local)"

    ```bash
    curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"provider": "ollama", "display_name": "Local Ollama", "base_url": "http://localhost:11434"}'
    ```

    Outbound URLs are validated against private and loopback ranges. For local development the operator sets `SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS=true`; keep it `false` in shared environments.

The response never contains the key. `has_api_key` tells you that one is stored:

```json
{
  "id": "864beb2b-32f1-4ee1-aa0c-ccdd1ba34948",
  "org_id": "35af6d8d-f874-4b2b-9222-122092075307",
  "project_id": null,
  "provider": "openai",
  "display_name": "OpenAI prod",
  "has_api_key": true,
  "base_url": null,
  "api_version": null,
  "extra_config": {},
  "is_default": false,
  "is_verified": false,
  "verified_at": null,
  "key_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:35.717955",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:35.717957"
}
```

## Test and verify

You can test a key **before** saving it. This makes a one token request and is rate limited per user:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider": "openai", "api_key": "<key>", "model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"}'
# {"success": true, "latency_ms": 380, "model_used": "gpt-4o-mini", "error": null}
```

After saving, **verify** the stored credential. Runtime only uses verified credentials.

Verification sends a one token request to the model named in `extra_config.test_model`. Without it, `openai` and `azure_openai` use `gpt-4o-mini`, `deepseek` uses `deepseek-chat` and `ollama` uses `llama3`. **`openai_compatible` providers (Groq, Gemini, Claude, Cloudflare, custom) have no default**: verification fails with "No test model configured" until you set `extra_config.test_model`. For Azure, use a deployment name that exists in your resource.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/$CRED_ID/verify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

```json
{"success": false, "is_verified": false, "verified_at": null, "latency_ms": null, "error": "Authentication failed — check your API key"}
```

Changing `api_key` or `base_url` resets verification, so verify again after a rotation.

List the models a credential offers (providers that support listing return names; for the others `supports_listing` is `false` and you type the model name):

```bash
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/$CRED_ID/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
# {"models": ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini", "text-embedding-3-small"], "supports_listing": true}
```

## Manage credentials

| Action | Request |
|---|---|
| List | `GET /llm-providers/credentials` |
| Get one | `GET /llm-providers/credentials/{id}` |
| Rename, rotate key or change URL | `PUT /llm-providers/credentials/{id}` with only the fields to change |
| Mark as the default of its scope | `POST /llm-providers/credentials/{id}/set-default` |
| Delete | `DELETE /llm-providers/credentials/{id}` |

## Choose the model: attachments

A **model attachment** pins a `(credential, model_name)` pair to a target. There are three targets.

| Target | Endpoint | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Agent | `/llm-providers/model-attachments/agents/{agent_id}` | Only that agent |
| Project | `/llm-providers/model-attachments/projects/{project_id}` | Agents in that project without their own attachment |
| Organization | `/llm-providers/model-attachments/org` | Agents everywhere without a closer attachment |

Each target supports `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE`. The credential must be verified or `PUT` returns `422`.

```bash
# Organization default model
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"gpt-4o-mini\"}"

# A stronger model for one agent
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/agents/$AGENT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"gpt-4o\"}"
```

## Which model runs

For every execution Archy walks this list and uses the first tier that applies:

1. **Agent attachment**.
2. **Agent config pin**: `config.model` with both `credential_id` and `model_name`.
3. **Project attachment**.
4. **Project platform default model** (see below).
5. **Organization attachment**.
6. **Organization platform default model**.
7. **Legacy agent `model_name`** with no credential. This runs on the platform's own model service, not on your credential.

If none of these applies, the agent has no model and the call fails (or answers in echo mode, see [Agents](agents.md#talk-to-an-agent)). Agents built by the platform itself fall back to the operator's default model through tier 7.

A tier is skipped when its credential is missing or unverified. A stored credential that cannot be decrypted is an error, never a silent fallback. A project platform default model (tier 4) wins over an organization attachment (tier 5). The [flow diagram](../architecture/flows.md#which-model-runs) shows the same logic.

!!! warning "`is_default` does not choose the model"
    The `is_default` flag marks a credential as the default of its scope in the credential list, but **only attachments decide which model runs** for organization and project defaults. Always create an attachment.

!!! warning "Do not set only `config.model.model_name`"
    An agent whose `config.model` has a `model_name` but no `credential_id` does not pin a model. If a project or organization attachment (or a platform default model) exists, that wins and the agent's `model_name` is ignored. Otherwise the agent runs `model_name` on the platform model service, not on your provider. To pin a model to one agent use an agent attachment, or set both `credential_id` and `model_name`.

### Platform default model overrides
