Organizations that use the platform's hosted model (no credential) can still pick the deployment name. These tiers, and tier 7, run only when the organization allows the platform fallback (`allow_platform_llm_fallback`); otherwise the call fails with a `credential_error`.

| Scope | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Organization | `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE /llm-providers/platform-default-model` with `{"model_name": "..."}` |
| Project | `.../platform-default-model/projects/{project_id}` |

### When nothing is configured

If an organization has no usable credential and the platform fallback is disabled for it, execution fails with a clear message instead of using a shared key:

```json
{
  "mode": "credential_error",
  "credential_error": "No LLM provider credential is configured for this organization and platform fallback is disabled. Add an LLM provider credential ..."
}
```

Add and verify a credential, attach a model, and retry. This is not an authentication error; `401` always means the bearer token is bad.

## Embeddings

Knowledge bases embed text with a model from one of your credentials. Set the organization default once; each new knowledge base created without its own `embedding_model` copies it, so changing the default later never invalidates vectors that already exist.

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"credential_id\": \"$CRED_ID\", \"model_name\": \"text-embedding-3-small\", \"dimensions\": 1536}"
```

- Providers with embeddings: `azure_openai`, `openai`, `openai_compatible`, `ollama`. DeepSeek has no embeddings endpoint.
- `GET` returns the default with `available: false` if its credential was deleted or is no longer verified; new knowledge bases then fail until you change or clear it (`DELETE`).
- A knowledge base can also name its own model: `embedding_model: "connection:<credential_id>:<model_name>"`.

## A helper in Python

```python
import httpx


def connect_openai(client: httpx.Client, api_key: str) -> str:
    """Create, verify and attach an OpenAI credential as the organization default. Returns its id."""
    cred = client.post(
        "/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials",
        json={"provider": "openai", "display_name": "OpenAI", "api_key": api_key},
    )
    cred.raise_for_status()
    cred_id = cred.json()["id"]

    check = client.post(f"/api/v1/llm-providers/credentials/{cred_id}/verify").json()
    if not check["success"]:
        raise RuntimeError(check["error"])

    for url, body in (
        ("/api/v1/llm-providers/model-attachments/org", {"credential_id": cred_id, "model_name": "gpt-4o-mini"}),
        (
            "/api/v1/llm-providers/embedding-default",
            {"credential_id": cred_id, "model_name": "text-embedding-3-small", "dimensions": 1536},
        ),
    ):
        client.put(url, json=body).raise_for_status()
    return cred_id
```

## Security notes

- Keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Each credential records the `key_id` it was encrypted under, so operators can rotate encryption keys without downtime.
- Responses and logs never include the key. Provide it only when creating or rotating.
- `base_url` values are validated against SSRF rules before any request leaves the platform.
- Credentials are tenant scoped. An organization can never resolve another organization's credential.


<!-- source: guides/knowledge-bases.md -->
# Knowledge bases

A **knowledge base** (KB) is a collection of documents that Archy splits into chunks, embeds with your embedding model and stores in a vector index. Agents and your own code retrieve the most relevant chunks for a question (retrieval-augmented generation, RAG).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SRC[Files, URLs, Confluence] --> ING[Ingest]
    ING --> ST[(Object storage)]
    ING --> JOB[Indexing job]
    JOB --> CH[Extract and chunk]
    CH --> EMB[Embed]
    EMB --> VEC[(Vector index)]
    Q[Question] --> RET[Retrieve top-k]
    VEC --> RET
    RET --> AG[Agent or your code]
```

!!! info "Before you start"
    You need a verified LLM credential and an [embedding default](llm-providers.md#embeddings), or a KB with its own `embedding_model`. All paths below start with `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}`.

```bash
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"
```

## Create a knowledge base

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "handbook", "description": "Company handbook"}'
```

```json
{
  "id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "name": "handbook",
  "description": "Company handbook",
  "embedding_model": "connection:864beb2b-32f1-4ee1-aa0c-ccdd1ba34948:text-embedding-3-small",
  "vector_store_config": {"dimensions": 1536}
}
```

With an organization embedding default the response shows the copied `connection:<credential_id>:<model>` value and may add the vector `dimensions`. Without a default both are `null`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | 1 to 255 characters |
| `description` | Optional |
| `embedding_model` | Optional. Defaults to the organization embedding default. Use `connection:<credential_id>:<model_name>` to pin one. |
| `vector_store_config` | Optional vector store options, for example the vector `dimensions` |

Choose the embedding model **before** you add documents. Vectors made with one model cannot be searched with another.

## Add documents

### Upload files

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/upload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -F "files=@handbook.pdf" -F "files=@faq.md"
```

Supported types: `.txt`, `.md`, `.json`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`. Other extensions (for example `.csv`, `.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt`) are rejected with `400 Unsupported file type`. Each file may be up to 50 MB. An unsupported type or an oversized file is rejected for the whole request.

The response lists the created documents, normally with `status: "uploaded"`, and indexing is queued automatically. Without a job queue the upload indexes synchronously before it returns, so a document can already be `indexed` or `failed`.

### Import from URLs

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/from-urls" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls": ["https://example.com/pricing", "https://example.com/terms"]}'
```

You can send up to 20 URLs. The response is a partial success: `documents` for the pages that were fetched and `errors` (`url` and `detail`) for the ones that failed. URLs pass the same SSRF validation as every outbound request.

### Import from Confluence

Confluence pages are read with a personal Atlassian connection that you create once (see [Connections and integrations](../reference/connections.md)). Pass its id:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/documents/from-confluence" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"integration_id\": \"$INTEGRATION_ID\", \"page_urls\": [\"https://acme.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123/Runbook\"], \"include_children\": true, \"max_depth\": 3}"
```

For large spaces use the background import (`POST .../confluence-imports`) and refresh later with `POST .../sources/{source_id}/confluence-sync`. Each import is tracked as a **source**; `GET .../sources` lists them and `POST .../sources/{source_id}/sync` re-syncs one.

## Index

After an upload Archy indexes each document in the background. You can also drive it yourself.

| Goal | Request |
|---|---|
| Index every document (async) | `POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/index` |
| Index every document and wait | `POST .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/index-sync` |
| Index one document (async job) | `POST .../documents/{doc}/index-jobs` |
| Poll one job | `GET .../documents/{doc}/index-jobs/{job}` |
| Summary of the whole KB | `GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/stats` |

```bash
curl -s "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/stats" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

```json
{"files_total": 12, "indexed_total": 10, "indexing_total": 2}
```

A job has `status` `queued`, `running`, `succeeded` or `failed`; a failed job reports `error_type` and `error_message`. A document's own `status` moves `uploaded`, `indexing`, `indexed` or `failed`. `POST .../index` re-queues **every** document of the knowledge base (each document has at most one job, which is reset) and returns `503` when the queue is unavailable. `POST .../index-sync` processes only documents that are not yet `indexed` and waits for the result.

## Query

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/knowledge-bases/$KB_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?", "top_k": 5, "retrieval_strategy": "hybrid"}'
```

```json
{
  "kb_id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
  "query": "How long do I have to ask for a refund?",
  "results": [
    {
      "chunk_id": "c1f0...",
      "score": 0.83,
      "content": "Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.",
      "metadata": {"filename": "handbook.md"}
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `query` | 1 to 20,000 characters |
| `top_k` | 1 to 50, default 5 |
| `retrieval_strategy` | `hybrid` (default: vector plus lexical), `vector` (similarity only), `graph` (expands results by shared entities for multi-hop questions) |

## Use a knowledge base from an agent

Set the KB in the agent config. The agent retrieves context before it answers.

```json
{
  "name": "support-assistant",
  "config": {
    "sys_prompt": "Answer only from the knowledge base. Say when you do not know.",
    "knowledge_base_id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
    "knowledge_base_top_k": 4
  }
}
```

`POST .../agents/{agent_id}/query` with `{"kb_id", "query", "top_k", "min_score"}` is a **retrieval preview**, not a model call: it streams NDJSON events `agent_start`, `retrieval` (the retrieved chunks) and `agent_final`, whose `response` joins the retrieved chunks. It does not use the agent's model or configuration. To get a model answer, query the agent normally ([Running and streaming](running-and-streaming.md)).

## Manage

| Action | Request |
|---|---|
| List knowledge bases | `GET .../knowledge-bases` |
| Usage across knowledge bases | `GET .../knowledge-bases/usage` |
| List documents | `GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents` |
| Delete a document | `DELETE .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/documents/{doc}` |
| Export metadata, sources and documents | `GET .../knowledge-bases/{kb}/export` |
| Delete a knowledge base | `DELETE .../knowledge-bases/{kb}` |

## Python: upload and wait

```python
import time
import httpx


def add_files_and_wait(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, kb_id: str, paths: list[str], timeout: int = 600) -> dict:
    files = [("files", (p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1], open(p, "rb"))) for p in paths]
    client.post(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/documents/upload", files=files).raise_for_status()

    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        stats = client.get(f"{scope}/knowledge-bases/{kb_id}/stats").json()
        if stats["indexing_total"] == 0 and stats["files_total"] > 0:
            return stats
        time.sleep(2)
    raise TimeoutError("indexing did not finish")


# scope = f"/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}"
```

If `indexed_total` is lower than `files_total` after `indexing_total` reaches `0`, some documents failed: list them with `GET .../documents` and look at `status`.

## Practices that improve answers

- **One knowledge base per subject.** Mixing unrelated material lowers precision. Attach several KBs through [workflows](composite-workflows.md#attach-resources) when an agent needs more than one.
- **Test retrieval first.** Call `/query` with real questions and read the chunks before you blame the agent prompt.
- **Keep `top_k` small.** 3 to 8 chunks is usually enough; more adds noise and cost.
- **Prefer text-rich sources.** Scanned images contain less retrievable text than PDFs with a text layer.
- **Do not change the embedding model of a populated KB.** Create a new KB and re-ingest instead.
- **Tell the agent what to do when the answer is missing.** "Say you do not know" in the system prompt prevents invented answers.


<!-- source: guides/agents.md -->
# Agents

An **agent** is a stored configuration that Archy turns into a reasoning-and-acting (ReAct) agent at run time. It reads the conversation, optionally retrieves from a knowledge base, calls tools and answers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CFG[Agent config] --> RT[Agent runtime]
    MODEL[Resolved model] --> RT
    KB[Knowledge base] --> RT
    MCP[MCP tools] --> RT
    SK[Skills] --> RT
    MEM[Memory] --> RT
    RT --> OUT[Answer, tool calls, session history]
```

## Create an agent

Project agents live in `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents`. Organization agents live in `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/agents` and are visible from every project of the organization.

```bash
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "support-assistant",
    "description": "Answers support questions",
    "config": {
      "sys_prompt": "You are a support assistant. Answer from the knowledge base and say when you do not know.",
      "knowledge_base_id": "7da160d1-8924-4b11-8442-6bd722deccc8",
      "knowledge_base_top_k": 4,
      "temperature": 0.2,
      "memory": {"mode": "buffer", "window_messages": 20}
    }
  }'
```

```json
{
  "id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e",
  "org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865",
  "scope": "project",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "name": "support-assistant",
  "description": "Answers support questions",
  "type": null,
  "config": {"sys_prompt": "...", "knowledge_base_id": "...", "knowledge_base_top_k": 4, "temperature": 0.2, "memory": {"mode": "buffer"}},
  "avatar_path": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:19:16.984748",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:19:16.984750"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Required, 1 to 255 characters |
| `description` | Optional text |
| `type` | Optional label, up to 50 characters |
| `config` | The runtime configuration, described below |

### Manage agents

| Action | Request |
|---|---|
| List | `GET .../agents` |
| Get | `GET .../agents/{agent_id}` |
| Update | `PUT .../agents/{agent_id}` |
| Delete | `DELETE .../agents/{agent_id}` (returns `{"status": "deleted"}`) |

!!! note "Stored config"
    Default values are not stored: for example `"window_messages": 20` is dropped from a `memory` object. If the operator configured a default agent model, `config.model` is filled in when you omit it.

!!! warning "`PUT` replaces `config`"
    An update with a `config` object **replaces the whole configuration**; it is not merged. Read the agent first, change what you need and send the complete object. Fields you omit at the top level (`name`, `description`, `type`) are left unchanged.

## The configuration

The `config` object is validated when you save it. An unknown key or a wrong type returns `400`:

```json
{
  "detail": {
    "message": "Invalid config",
    "errors": [{"type": "extra_forbidden", "loc": ["bogus"], "msg": "Extra inputs are not permitted"}]
  }
}
```

### Core

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_prompt` | string | The system prompt. Aliases `instructions` and `system_prompt` are accepted. Default: `You are a helpful assistant.` |
| `model` | object | `{provider, model_name, credential_id}`. See [Which model runs](llm-providers.md#which-model-runs). Prefer attachments over this field. |
| `temperature` | number 0 to 2 | Sampling temperature |
| `top_p` | number 0 to 1 | Nucleus sampling |
| `max_tokens` | integer ≥ 1 | Maximum tokens of one model reply |
| `max_iters` | integer 1 to 100 | Maximum reasoning and tool iterations per reply |
| `token_budget` | integer ≥ 1 | Overall token budget of one reply |
| `input_token_weight`, `output_token_weight` | number ≥ 0 | Weights used when counting against the budget |

### Knowledge and tools

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `knowledge_base_id` | UUID | Knowledge base used for retrieval |
| `knowledge_base_top_k` | integer ≥ 1 | Chunks retrieved per question |
| `tools_enabled` | list of strings | Stored tool labels. They are not used by the agent runtime; retrieval is driven by `knowledge_base_id`. |
| `skills_enabled` | list of strings | Skills to attach |
| `automatic_mcp` | boolean | Connect the MCP servers attached to the agent automatically. When unset it is off, unless the agent has a personal integration grant, in which case it is on. |
| `web_search` | object | `{enabled, provider: duckduckgo or tavily or brave, api_key}` |
| `playwright` | object | `{enabled, headless}` browser automation tool |
| `deep_research` | object | `{enabled, max_iterations (1-50), max_depth (1-10), search_provider, tavily_api_key}` |

### Memory

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `memory` | object | `{mode, window_messages}` with `mode` one of `none`, `buffer`, `agentscope_db`, `in_memory`, `sqlalchemy`, `redis` |
| `memory_window` | integer 0 to 50 | Number of previous messages replayed |
| `long_term_memory` | object | `{enabled, mode: static_control or agent_control or both, provider: qdrant}`; facts survive across sessions |

### Advanced

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `model_routing` | object | Per-reply routing: a `router_model` picks one of `candidates` (`name`, `model`, `description`) by the latest user message. Needs at least one candidate when enabled. |
| `structured_output` | boolean | Ask the agent to return structured output |
| `allowed_agent_ids`, `default_participant_agent_ids` | list of UUID strings | Used by multi-agent dialog orchestration |
| `hooks_enabled` | list of strings | Lifecycle hooks to enable |
| `voice`, `elevenlabs_voice_id` | string | Voice settings for realtime conversations |
| `external` | object | Free-form metadata for provisioning systems |

## Talk to an agent

### One request, one answer

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "What are your support hours?"}'
```

```json
{
  "agent_id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e",
  "session_id": "4e7c87f4-30d4-565f-a47b-9b4fca7f385a",
  "output": "Support hours are 08:00 to 18:00 CET, Monday to Friday.",
  "meta": {}
}
```

A **session** stores the conversation. Omit `session_id` to start a new one. Pass it back to continue:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"message\": \"And on weekends?\", \"session_id\": \"$SESSION_ID\"}"
```

An unknown `session_id` returns `404`.

!!! warning "No model resolved"
    If no model can be resolved for the agent (no attachment, no pinned credential and no platform default), the API may answer in **echo mode** instead of failing: `output` is `Echo: <your message>` and `meta.mode` is `echo` (or `rag+echo` when the agent has a knowledge base) with a `fallback_reason` such as `missing_agent_model_config`. When a credential cannot be used, `meta.mode` is `credential_error` and `meta.credential_error` explains why. In every case [connect and attach a model](llm-providers.md#choose-the-model-attachments). In automated tests assert that `meta.mode` is none of `echo`, `rag+echo` and `credential_error`.

### Stream the answer

For chat interfaces use Server-Sent Events. Events are `start`, repeated `delta`, then `end` (or `error`). See [Running and streaming](running-and-streaming.md) for parsers.

```bash
curl -N -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/chat/stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Summarize our refund policy"}'
```

## Give the agent more abilities

- **Knowledge**: set `knowledge_base_id` (see [Knowledge bases](knowledge-bases.md)).
- **Tools from MCP servers**: register a server and attach it to the agent (see [External MCP servers and skills](mcp-servers-for-agents.md)).
- **Skills**: attach a skill with `POST .../agents/{agent_id}/skills`.
- **Another model**: attach one with [model attachments](llm-providers.md#choose-the-model-attachments).
- **Personal Atlassian access**: grant a connection to the agent with the `integration-grants` endpoints.

## State, memory and plans

| Capability | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Session state | `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/state` |
| Cross-session memory summaries | `GET .../agents/{agent_id}/memory` |
| Multi-step plans | `POST` and `GET /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/plans`, `PUT` and `DELETE .../plans/{plan_id}` |
| Avatar | `PUT` and `GET .../agents/{agent_id}/avatar` |
| Audit of an agent | `GET /api/v1/agents/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_id}/audit` |

## Write a good system prompt

- State the role and the audience in the first sentence.
- Say what the agent must do when it lacks information ("ask a clarifying question", "say you do not know").
- Name the sources it may use. For a knowledge base agent: "Answer only from the knowledge base."
- Describe the format of the answer (length, language, bullet list, JSON).
- Put **business rules in the prompt, not in your code.** Archy is domain neutral; your prompt is where your product's behavior lives.

## Python: create and chat

```python
import httpx


def create_agent(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, name: str, prompt: str, kb_id: str | None = None) -> str:
    config = {"sys_prompt": prompt, "memory": {"mode": "buffer", "window_messages": 20}}
    if kb_id:
        config["knowledge_base_id"] = kb_id
    r = client.post(f"{scope}/agents", json={"name": name, "config": config})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["id"]


def chat(client: httpx.Client, agent_id: str) -> None:
    session_id = None
    while (message := input("you> ")) not in ("", "quit"):
        body = {"message": message, **({"session_id": session_id} if session_id else {})}
        r = client.post(f"/api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query", json=body, timeout=120)
        r.raise_for_status()
        reply = r.json()
        session_id = reply["session_id"]
        print("agent>", reply["output"])
```


<!-- source: guides/workflows.md -->
# Workflows

A **workflow** coordinates several agents (and sometimes tools and other workflows) to complete a task that one agent cannot do alone. Archy supports two families:

- **Legacy typed workflows** (this page): choose a pattern such as `sequential` or `debate` and list the agents. Quick to set up.
- **Composite workflows** ([next page](composite-workflows.md)): a graph of nodes and edges with inputs, variables, conditions, loops, human checkpoints and file output. Use it when you need control.

Workflows live in `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/workflows` (or `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workflows` for organization scope). Every `PUT` that leaves the workflow with a config stores a snapshot as a new **version** you can list and read (creating a workflow does not). Organization-scope workflows support only create, list, get and `execute`; everything else on this page is project-scoped.

## Create a workflow

```bash
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{
    \"name\": \"draft-and-edit\",
    \"description\": \"A writer drafts, an editor improves\",
    \"type\": \"sequential\",
    \"config\": {\"agent_ids\": [\"$WRITER_ID\", \"$EDITOR_ID\"]}
  }"
```

```json
{
  "id": "313bacab-956b-4366-8f82-f134407f0d61",
  "org_id": "84eab6dd-2cc1-41d9-a5e7-0c5e38197865",
  "project_id": "f834cf48-7bf7-4489-8b4b-9c7d8c832cb5",
  "scope": "project",
  "name": "draft-and-edit",
  "description": "A writer drafts, an editor improves",
  "type": "sequential",
  "config": {"agent_ids": ["26fc2a0e-...", "dd7b220d-..."]},
  "legacy_history": false,
  "executable": true
}
```

The `config` is validated against the type. A violation returns `422`:

```json
{"detail": [{"type": "value_error", "loc": ["body"], "msg": "Value error, config.agent_ids is required"}]}
```

## Workflow types

| `type` | Pattern | Required `config` |
|---|---|---|
| `sequential` | Agents run one after another; each receives the previous output | `agent_ids` (list) |
| `parallel` | All agents work on the same input at once; outputs are combined | `agent_ids` |
| `dialog` | Agents take turns in a conversation | `agent_ids`, optional `turns` (1 to 100) |
| `conversation` | Multi-agent conversation over a shared message hub | `agent_ids` (at least 2), optional `turns` (1 to 200) |
| `routing` | A router agent, keyword routes or a default agent decide who handles the request (see below) | `default_agent_id`; optional `router_agent_id`, `routes`, `route_map`, `routing_tool_names` |
| `orchestrator` | A manager delegates to workers, or a RAG orchestrator compares two knowledge bases | `manager_agent_id` and `worker_agent_ids`, **or** `kb_a_id` and `kb_b_id` (optional `top_k` 1 to 50) |
| `business-pipeline` | Business agents first, then pipeline agents | `business_agent_ids`, `pipeline_agent_ids`, optional `business_mode` (`parallel` or `sequential`) |
| `staged` | Ordered stages, each parallel or sequential, optionally fanned in | `stages` (list of `{agent_ids, mode, name}`), optional `fanin` |
| `handoff` | Workers (agents, tools or sub-workflows) are selected by keyword matches | `workers` (at least 2) with `kind` `agent`, `tool` or `sub_workflow`; optional `max_workers` |
| `debate` | Solver agents argue for several rounds and a moderator decides | `solver_agent_ids` (at least 2), `moderator_agent_id`, optional `rounds` (1 to 20) |
| `interactive-orchestrator` | Multi-turn orchestration with one manager | `manager_agent_id`; optional `knowledge_base_id`, `structured_output_schema` |
| `composite` | A graph definition | See [Composite workflow graphs](composite-workflows.md) |
| `two-agent` | Legacy; only used by the two-agent SSE endpoint | none |

A workflow with no `type` is treated as `sequential`.

!!! info "Read-only legacy rows"
    Old history rows of types `intake_generation`, `backlog_refine`, `backlog_enhance` and `backlog_split` can still be listed. They show `executable: false` and `legacy_history: true`, and new ones can no longer be created.

### Sequential step input

By default a sequential step only sees the previous step's output. To also give every step the original assignment, set:

```json
{
  "agent_ids": ["...", "..."],
  "step_input_mode": "assignment_plus_previous",
  "handoff_instructions": "Keep the tone formal."
}
```

`step_input_mode` is `previous_output` (default) or `assignment_plus_previous`. `handoff_instructions` is text of at most 8000 characters that is appended to each step's input when `step_input_mode` is `assignment_plus_previous` (it is ignored otherwise).

### Require MCP servers

For `sequential` and `composite` workflows you can fail fast when a tool server is down:

```json
{"agent_ids": ["..."], "required_mcp_servers": ["jira", "confluence"]}
```

When a listed server is not connected the node fails with `MCP_UNAVAILABLE` and the run fails.

### How routing and handoff decide

**Routing** decides in this order: (1) the router agent (`router_agent_id`) replies with JSON `{"route": "<key>"}`, a key of `route_map`, or `{"agent_id": "<uuid>"}` (a tool call also works when `routing_tool_names` is set); (2) otherwise `routes` entries `{contains, agent_id}` are matched case-insensitively against the message; (3) otherwise `default_agent_id` handles it. Without a `router_agent_id` there is no model-based routing.

**Handoff** first picks the workers whose `matches` keywords appear in the message (case-insensitive), then fills up to `max_workers` (default 2) with the remaining workers in configuration order. Every selected worker runs. `kind` defaults to `agent`; `kind: tool` supports only the built-in test tools `echo`, `uppercase` and `fail`.

### Examples

=== "Routing"

    ```json
    {
      "name": "triage",
      "type": "routing",
      "config": {
        "router_agent_id": "<router agent>",
        "default_agent_id": "<general agent>",
        "route_map": {"billing": "<billing agent>", "technical": "<tech agent>"}
      }
    }
    ```

=== "Debate"

    ```json
    {
      "name": "decision",
      "type": "debate",
      "config": {
        "solver_agent_ids": ["<optimist>", "<skeptic>"],
        "moderator_agent_id": "<moderator>",
        "rounds": 3
      }
    }
    ```

=== "Staged"

    ```json
    {
      "name": "report",
      "type": "staged",
      "config": {
        "stages": [
          {"name": "collect", "mode": "parallel", "agent_ids": ["<a>", "<b>"]},
          {"name": "write", "mode": "sequential", "agent_ids": ["<writer>"]}
        ]
      }
    }
    ```

=== "Handoff"

    ```json
    {
      "name": "support-desk",
      "type": "handoff",
      "config": {
        "workers": [
          {"kind": "agent", "agent_id": "<billing>", "matches": ["invoice", "refund"]},
          {"kind": "agent", "agent_id": "<tech>", "matches": ["error", "crash"]}
        ],
        "max_workers": 1
      }
    }
    ```

## Manage workflows

| Action | Request |
|---|---|
| List | `GET .../workflows` |
| Get | `GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}` |
| Update | `PUT .../workflows/{workflow_id}`; a new version is stored |
| Delete | `DELETE .../workflows/{workflow_id}` |
| List versions | `GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/versions` |
| Read a version | `GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/versions/{version_number}` |
| Mark a version active | `POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/versions/{version_number}/activate` (changes the active flag only, not the config that runs; to roll back, read the version and `PUT` its `config`) |
| Usage per workflow | `GET .../workflows/usage` |

## Run a workflow

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Write a short note about our new refund policy"}'
```

```json
{
  "session_id": "5c9ef9bb-4dd5-4c14-b2ac-0f93f4b5f4d1",
  "output": "...",
  "structured_output": null,
  "audit": [{"agent": "writer", "...": "..."}],
  "error": null,
  "status": "completed",
  "pending_input": null
}
```

The response has the final `output` and an `audit` trail of the steps. Streaming and asynchronous runs are covered in [Running and streaming](running-and-streaming.md).

Useful request options (all optional except `message`):

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | Continue a session, or resume a run paused at a checkpoint |
| `inputs` | Values for the inputs a composite workflow declares |
| `structured_output_schema` | JSON Schema; the final result is validated and returned as `structured_output` |
| `knowledge_base_id_override` | Use another knowledge base for this run |
| `mcp_enabled`, `mcp_tool_allowlist` | Turn MCP tools off or restrict them for this run only |
| `instructions_overlay` | Extra per-turn context for interactive orchestrators |

## Convert a legacy workflow to a graph

`POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/convert-to-composite` returns `{type, config, acknowledged_losses}` for the equivalent composite graph without saving it. Types with no conversion return `400`. If the conversion would drop settings or merge a repeated agent it fails with `CONVERSION_LOSSES` and lists them; call it again with `{"acknowledge_losses": true}` once you accept them. Validate the result and save it with `PUT` using `"type": "composite"` and the returned `config`. See [Composite workflow graphs](composite-workflows.md#validate-before-you-save).

## Choosing a type

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q{What do you need?}
    Q -->|A fixed pipeline| S[sequential]
    Q -->|Independent opinions at once| P[parallel]
    Q -->|Pick the right specialist| R[routing or handoff]
    Q -->|Stages with fan-out and fan-in| ST[staged]
    Q -->|A manager and workers| O[orchestrator]
    Q -->|Challenge and decide| D[debate]
    Q -->|Conditions, loops, human approval, files| C[composite]
```


<!-- source: guides/composite-workflows.md -->
# Composite workflow graphs

A **composite workflow** is a graph: typed **nodes** joined by typed **edges**, plus declared **inputs** and **variables**. It can branch on conditions, loop, run branches in parallel, merge results, pause for a human, call other workflows and save files.

This page teaches by building graphs. The authoritative, always current contracts are served by the API (and as MCP tools), so read them when you generate graphs programmatically:

| Contract | REST | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| Authoring guide (Markdown) | `GET /api/v1/workflow-authoring-guide` | `workflow_authoring_guide_get` |
| Node type registry | `GET /api/v1/workflow-node-types` | `workflow_node_types_get` |
| JSON Schema of the definition | `GET /api/v1/workflow-definition-schema` | `workflow_definition_schema_get` |
| Validation and run error codes | `GET /api/v1/workflow-validation-codes` | `workflow_validation_codes_get` |

## The definition

A composite workflow has `type: "composite"` and a `config` that is a version 2 definition:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "inputs": [],
  "variables": {},
  "graph": {"nodes": [], "edges": []}
}
```

- **Node**: `{id, type, data, position}`. `id` is unique. `data.name` is the reference name other nodes use as `nodes.<name>` (lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 48 characters). `position` is `{x, y}` and only matters for editors.
- **Edge**: `{id, source, target, sourceHandle?, targetHandle?, data?}`. The connection type is read from `data.connectionType`, default `sequential`.
- Exactly **one `start`** node and at least **one `end`** node. A path must lead from `start` to an `end` and no node may be left unconnected (`ORPHAN_NODE`); a node that `start` cannot reach is a warning (`UNREACHABLE_NODE`). A cycle is allowed only through a `loop` node.
- Unknown keys are preserved, so editors can store their own fields.

## Your first graph

Two agents in a row, with a declared input:

```json
{
  "name": "research-and-write",
  "type": "composite",
  "config": {
    "version": 2,
    "inputs": [{"name": "topic", "type": "string", "required": true}],
    "graph": {
      "nodes": [
        {"id": "start", "type": "start", "data": {}},
        {"id": "a1", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "researcher", "agentId": "<agent id>", "prompt": "Research: {{input.topic}}"}},
        {"id": "a2", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "writer", "agentId": "<agent id>", "prompt": "Write a summary of:\n{{nodes.researcher.output}}"}},
        {"id": "end", "type": "end", "data": {}}
      ],
      "edges": [
        {"id": "e1", "source": "start", "target": "a1"},
        {"id": "e2", "source": "a1", "target": "a2"},
        {"id": "e3", "source": "a2", "target": "end"}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S((start)) --> R[agent: researcher]
    R --> W[agent: writer]
    W --> E((end))
```

Create it with `POST .../workflows`, then run it:

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/execute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Research request", "inputs": {"topic": "vector databases"}}'
```

## Node types

| Type | Category | Purpose | Key `data` fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | terminal | Entry point | none |
| `end` | terminal | Exit point | none |
| `agent` | agent | Runs a configured agent | `agentId` (required), `name`, `prompt`, `role`, `outputSchema`, `required_mcp_servers` |
| `hub` | agent | Coordinates agents as a hub. Passes its input through at run time. | `agentId` (required), `name`, `prompt` |
| `msghub` | agent | Multi-agent conversation on a shared hub | `name`, `maxRounds`, `announcement` |
| `pipeline` | flow | Runs several agents sequentially or fanned out | `agentIds` (required), `mode` (`sequential` or `fanout`), `prompt`, `outputSchema` |
| `router` | flow | Declares labelled `route` branches. Passes its input through at run time: all outgoing edges run. Use `condition` to choose one. | `agentId` (required), `name`, `prompt` |
| `condition` | flow | Branches on a field comparison | `field`, `operator` (`equals`, `not_equals`, `contains`, `greater_than`), `value` |
| `loop` | flow | Repeats a body until a condition holds or the limit is reached | `conditionField` (required), `conditionValue`, `maxIterations` (required) |
| `merge` | flow | Combines parallel branches | `strategy` (`concatenate`, `summarize`, `pick_best`), `instruction`, `outputSchema` |
| `checkpoint` | flow | Pauses for human input | `prompt`, `timeoutSeconds` |
| `sub-workflow` | flow | Runs another workflow as a step | `workflowId` (required) |
| `save-file` | sink | Saves output as a file (artifact) | `source`, `format`, `fileName`, `overwrite` |
| `storage-read`, `storage-write`, `storage-list` | integration | Read, write and list files in a storage connection | `connectionId`, `location`, `parent`, ... |
| `satellite-mcp`, `satellite-kb`, `satellite-skill` | resource | Attach an MCP server, knowledge base or skill to an agent or pipeline | `satelliteType`, `resourceId`, `toolAllowlist` |

`GET /api/v1/workflow-node-types` returns the full registry: required fields, ports (handles) and which node types each node may connect to.

## Connection types

| `data.connectionType` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sequential` (default) | Run the target after the source |
| `consult` | An agent consults another agent |
| `handoff` | An agent hands the conversation over |
| `route` | A labelled branch out of a `condition` (or `router`); needs a label in `data.condition` |
| `attachment` | A resource node attached to an agent or pipeline; carries no data and schedules nothing |

## Patterns

### Route to a specialist

!!! warning "`router` and `hub` nodes pass their input through"
    At run time a `router` (and a `hub`) node does not call its agent or choose a branch: every outgoing edge runs. To send a request to one of two specialists, classify it with an agent that returns structured output and branch with a `condition` node ([Branch on a value](#branch-on-a-value)). For more than two branches chain `condition` nodes, or use the legacy [`routing` workflow type](workflows.md#how-routing-and-handoff-decide).

### Parallel branches and merge

Two edges leave `start`; a `merge` node combines the results. A merge needs at least two incoming branches.

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "pricing", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "b", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "legal", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "m", "type": "merge", "data": {"name": "combined", "strategy": "summarize"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "s", "target": "b"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "a", "target": "m", "targetHandle": "target-top-1"},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "b", "target": "m", "targetHandle": "target-top-2"},
    {"id": "e5", "source": "m", "target": "e"}
  ]
}
```

Strategies: `concatenate` joins the outputs, `summarize` asks a model to summarize them, `pick_best` chooses one. `maxConcurrency` (1 to 32, default 8) at the top of the definition limits how many agent and sub-workflow calls run at the same time.

### Branch on a value

Use structured output so the condition has a field to read.

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {
      "name": "classify", "agentId": "<agent>",
      "outputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"urgent": {"type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["urgent"]}
    }},
    {"id": "c", "type": "condition", "data": {"name": "gate", "field": "urgent", "operator": "equals", "value": "true"}},
    {"id": "x", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "escalate", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "y", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "normal", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "c"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "c", "target": "x", "sourceHandle": "source-true", "data": {"connectionType": "route", "condition": "yes"}},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "c", "target": "y", "sourceHandle": "source-false", "data": {"connectionType": "route", "condition": "no"}},
    {"id": "e5", "source": "x", "target": "e"},
    {"id": "e6", "source": "y", "target": "e"}
  ]
}
```

A condition needs at least two `route` edges with distinct labels. How it works at run time:

- `field` is a **key of the incoming JSON object**, which is the output of the upstream node (use `outputSchema` so the agent returns JSON). It is not a template: `{{nodes.classify.json.urgent}}` would be rendered first and its result used as the key, which never matches. Leave `field` empty to compare the whole input text.
- `operator` is `equals`, `not_equals`, `contains` or `greater_than`. Comparisons ignore case; `greater_than` compares numbers.
- When the condition holds, edges labelled `true` or `yes` run; otherwise edges labelled `false` or `no` run. An edge labelled `default` (or with no label) always runs. Any other label is accepted by validation but never taken. The label is `data.condition`, or `true`/`false` from `sourceHandle` `source-true`/`source-false` when no label is set.

### Loop until done

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "l", "type": "loop", "data": {"name": "refine", "conditionField": "done", "conditionValue": "true", "maxIterations": 3}},
    {"id": "w", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "rewrite", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "v", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "review", "agentId": "<agent>", "outputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"done": {"type": "boolean"}}}}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "l"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "l", "target": "w", "sourceHandle": "source-body"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "w", "target": "v"},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "v", "target": "l"},
    {"id": "e5", "source": "l", "target": "e", "sourceHandle": "source-exit"}
  ]
}
```

The body leaves from `source-body` and comes back to the loop node; the continuation leaves from `source-exit`. `conditionField` is a **key of the JSON output of the node that returns to the loop** (here the `review` agent's structured output), not a template. The loop exits when that value equals `conditionValue` (ignoring case). `maxIterations` must be above 0; it is clamped to 1 to 50 and defaults to 5.

### Pause for approval

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "draft", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "k", "type": "checkpoint", "data": {"name": "approval", "prompt": "Approve this draft?\n{{nodes.draft.output}}"}},
    {"id": "b", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "publish", "agentId": "<agent>", "prompt": "Finalize: {{nodes.draft.output}}\nReviewer said: {{nodes.approval.output}}"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "k"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "k", "target": "b"},
    {"id": "e4", "source": "b", "target": "e"}
  ]
}
```

The run stops with `status: "awaiting_input"` and the rendered prompt. The answer becomes the checkpoint node's output, here `{{nodes.approval.output}}`. See [Human approval checkpoint](../tutorials/human-approval.md).

### Attach resources

Give an agent a knowledge base, MCP server or skill by adding a resource node and an `attachment` edge from the resource to the agent:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "s", "type": "start", "data": {}},
    {"id": "a", "type": "agent", "data": {"name": "support", "agentId": "<agent>"}},
    {"id": "kb", "type": "satellite-kb", "data": {"satelliteType": "kb", "resourceId": "<knowledge base id>"}},
    {"id": "e", "type": "end", "data": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"id": "e1", "source": "s", "target": "a"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "a", "target": "e"},
    {"id": "e3", "source": "kb", "target": "a", "data": {"connectionType": "attachment"}}
  ]
}
```

- `resourceId` is the id of the knowledge base, MCP server or skill. `satelliteType` is `kb`, `mcp` or `skill` and must match the node type.
- For MCP you can add `toolAllowlist` (at most 100 unique tool names) to expose only some tools.
- Limits per target: 5 MCP servers and 3 knowledge bases. One resource node may serve several agents. Routers, hubs and message hubs take no attachments.

### Save a file

```json
{"id": "f", "type": "save-file", "data": {"name": "save", "format": "markdown", "fileName": "report", "source": "workflow_output"}}
```

Formats: `markdown`, `text`, `json`, `html`, `csv`, `docx`, `xlsx`. The node outputs the file as an [artifact](sessions-artifacts-usage.md#artifacts), also readable as `nodes.save.files`.

## Inputs, variables and expressions

Text fields of a node (for example `prompt`) accept `{{ expression }}`.

| Source | Reads |
|---|---|
| `input.<name>` | A declared run input. `input.message` is the run message. |
| `vars.<name>` | A value from `variables` |
| `nodes.<name>.output` | The text output of an earlier node |
| `nodes.<name>.json.<path>` | A field of a structured output, for example `nodes.classify.json.items[0].id` |
| `nodes.<name>.files` | Files an earlier node produced |
| `run`, `now`, `loop`, `item` | Run metadata, time, loop and item context |

Filters chain with `|`: `date`, `default`, `eq`, `first`, `gt`, `gte`, `if`, `join`, `json`, `last`, `length`, `lower`, `lt`, `lte`, `ne`, `not`, `number`, `replace`, `split`, `trim`, `truncate`, `upper`, `url_encode`. Example: `{{ input.topic | trim | upper }}`.

Rules:

- Reference only nodes that run **before** the node holding the expression, and only names that exist.
- `nodes.<name>.json.<path>` must lie inside that node's `outputSchema` when it has one.
- Declare inputs as `{name, type, required, default, description, sensitive}` with `type` `string`, `number`, `boolean` or `json`. `message` is reserved.
- A `sensitive` input is masked as `***` in stored traces. Do not use it in checkpoint prompts or file names.
- Invalid inputs at run time return `422` with `detail.code = WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID` and a list of `{name, code, message}`.

### Structured output

Set `data.outputSchema` (a JSON Schema subset) on an agent, pipeline or merge node to get validated JSON, readable as `nodes.<name>.json.<path>`. A result that does not match fails the node with `SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED` after the repair attempts, and a node error fails the run. On a `merge` node the schema applies only to the `summarize` and `pick_best` strategies (with `concatenate` it is ignored and validation warns `OUTPUT_SCHEMA_IGNORED`).

## Validate before you save

`POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/validate` checks a graph and returns every issue. Send an unsaved graph in the body, or an empty object to check the saved one. Add `"requireNames": true` to get `NODE_NAME_MISSING` warnings.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/validate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"graph": {"nodes": [], "edges": []}}'
```

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "errors": [
    {"code": "NO_START", "message": "Workflow must have exactly one start node", "severity": "error", "node_id": null, "edge_id": null, "input_name": null, "field": null},
    {"code": "NO_END", "message": "Workflow must have at least one end node", "severity": "error", "node_id": null, "edge_id": null, "input_name": null, "field": null}
  ],
  "warnings": [
    {"code": "EMPTY_WORKFLOW", "message": "Workflow has no executable nodes", "severity": "warning", "node_id": null, "edge_id": null, "input_name": null, "field": null}
  ]
}
```

Errors must be fixed before you run the workflow; warnings are advice. Saving rejects (`422`) invalid, reserved or duplicate node names, errors in the `inputs` declaration, invalid `outputSchema` values, invalid `required_mcp_servers` and attachment errors, and an unsupported or invalid definition. Graph-shape errors (start and end nodes, reachability, branches, agent references, template references) are **not** rejected at save time and surface when the run starts (for example `400 Composite workflow must have a Start node`), so always validate first. Common codes:

| Code | Meaning and fix |
|---|---|
| `NO_START`, `MULTIPLE_START`, `NO_END` | Exactly one start and at least one end |
| `START_UNREACHABLE_END` | Connect the graph so an end node is reachable |
| `ORPHAN_NODE` (error), `UNREACHABLE_NODE` (warning) | Connect the node or remove it |
| `CYCLE_OUTSIDE_LOOP` | Cycles are allowed only through a `loop` node |
| `NODE_NAME_INVALID`, `NODE_NAME_DUPLICATE`, `NODE_NAME_RESERVED` | Use a unique lowercase name that is not `input`, `item`, `loop`, `nodes`, `now`, `run` or `vars` |
| `AGENT_REF_MISSING` | An agent, router or hub node needs an `agentId` of an agent in this project |
| `CONDITION_BRANCHES`, `ROUTER_ROUTES` | Add route edges with distinct, non-empty labels |
| `MERGE_INPUTS` | A merge needs two or more incoming branches |
| `LOOP_BODY` | Set `conditionField` and `maxIterations` above 0 |
| `SCHEMA_INVALID` | `outputSchema` uses features outside the supported subset |
| `TEMPLATE_NODE_NOT_UPSTREAM` | A template reads `nodes.<name>` of a node that does not run before it. Reorder the graph or read an earlier node. |
| `MCP_UNAVAILABLE` (run) | A required MCP server was not connected |

The complete catalog with meanings, severities and fix hints is `GET /api/v1/workflow-validation-codes`.

!!! tip "Workflow for generating graphs"
    1. Read the node type registry and the definition schema.
    2. Draft the graph with one start and one end.
    3. Call `validate` with the draft in the body; fix every error; repeat until `valid` is true. Validation needs an existing workflow id in the path, so create a placeholder workflow first (for example with an empty graph) and update it when the draft is valid.
    4. Save with `POST` (new) or `PUT` (existing), then validate the saved workflow once more with an empty body.
    5. Run a test execution and inspect the trace.

## Run behaviour to know

- A node error **fails the run**. No later node starts and there are no error edges. The run status is `failed`, `error` is set and `output` is empty.
- An agent node only sees the output of its incoming edges. To pass the run message plus the previous result plus an instruction, set the target's `data.prompt`, for example `{{input.message}}` then `Previous result: {{nodes.<previous>.output}}`. The prompt replaces the node input.
- An edge `data.instructions` (legacy alias `instruction`) is rendered and appended to that edge's output for agent, sub-workflow, message hub and pipeline targets. A target's own non-empty `prompt` replaces the input, including the instruction.
- Top-level `required_mcp_servers` applies to every agent node (including agents a `hub` fans out to, but not agents inside `router` or `pipeline` nodes); `data.required_mcp_servers` adds servers for one node. If a required server is not connected the node fails with `MCP_UNAVAILABLE`. Without the list, an unreachable server is skipped.

## Storage nodes

`storage-read`, `storage-write` and `storage-list` use a storage connection (Google Drive, OneDrive or Dropbox) of the project.

- `data.connectionId` is a literal UUID, never a template.
- `storage-read` copies a file into an artifact and passes its input through. `storage-write` writes text or an earlier file into a folder and takes `conflict` of `fail` (default), `overwrite` or `new_version`. `storage-list` returns `{entries, nextCursor}`.
- Errors carry stable codes such as `storage_not_found`, `storage_permission_denied`, `storage_file_too_large` and `storage_path_not_allowed`, and never a file path.
- A connection without a root folder allows no write. For Google Drive the scope is `drive.file`: a node sees only files the app created or the user picked.

## Versions

Every `PUT` that leaves the workflow with a config stores a version snapshot (creating does not).

```bash
curl -s "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/versions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/versions/2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

`POST .../versions/{n}/activate` only changes which version is flagged active; it does not change the config that runs. To roll back, read the old version and `PUT` its `config` back.

## Python: create, validate, run

```python
import httpx


def deploy_graph(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, name: str, config: dict) -> str:
    """Create the workflow, then refuse to use it when validation reports errors."""
    created = client.post(f"{scope}/workflows", json={"name": name, "type": "composite", "config": config})
    created.raise_for_status()
    workflow_id = created.json()["id"]

    report = client.post(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/validate", json={}).json()
    if not report["valid"]:
        client.delete(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}")
        raise ValueError([f"{e['code']}: {e['message']}" for e in report["errors"]])
    return workflow_id


def run(client: httpx.Client, scope: str, workflow_id: str, message: str, **inputs) -> dict:
    r = client.post(
        f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/execute",
        json={"message": message, "inputs": inputs or None},
        timeout=300,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()
```


<!-- source: guides/running-and-streaming.md -->
# Running and streaming

Archy offers three ways to execute an agent or workflow. Pick by what your caller can do.

| Mode | Use when | Agent | Workflow |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Synchronous** | Short tasks; you can wait for the final result | `POST /agents/{id}/query` | `POST .../workflows/{id}/execute` |
| **Streaming** | A UI should show progress as it happens | `POST .../agents/{id}/chat/stream` (SSE) | `POST .../workflows/{id}/execute/stream` (SSE) |
| **Asynchronous** | Your caller cannot hold a connection open (serverless, Atlassian Forge, queues) | | `POST .../workflows/{id}/runs`, then `GET .../runs/{run_id}` |

All requests need a bearer token ([Authentication](authentication.md)).

## Server-Sent Events (SSE)

Streaming endpoints respond with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Each event is two lines and a blank line:

```text
event: delta
data: {"delta": "Support hours are "}

```

!!! warning "Use `fetch`, not `EventSource`"
    Browsers' `EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header or a POST body. Read the stream with `fetch` and a `ReadableStream`, or let your backend relay it.

### Agent chat stream

`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_id}/chat/stream` with `{"message": "...", "session_id": "..."}`.

| Event | `data` |
|---|---|
| `start` | `{"agent_id", "session_id"}` |
| `delta` | `{"delta": "<text chunk>"}`, repeated |
| `end` | `{"agent_id", "session_id", "output", "meta"}` |
| `error` | `{"error": "execution_failed", "detail": "..."}` |

The `error` event replaces `end`. Handle it: the HTTP status is already `200` when it is sent.

!!! note "`delta` events are chunks of a finished answer"
    The agent runs to completion first; `delta` events then deliver the final output in chunks of about 20 characters. There is no token-level streaming, so the first `delta` arrives only after the agent has finished. Use the stream to render text progressively, and show your own progress indicator until the first `delta` arrives. `POST /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/query/stream` is a test stub that echoes the message; do not use it.

=== "curl"

    ```bash
    curl -N -X POST "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID/agents/$AGENT_ID/chat/stream" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"message": "Summarize our refund policy"}'
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    import json
    import os

    import httpx


    def sse_events(response: httpx.Response):
        """Yield (event, data) pairs from an SSE response."""
        event, data_lines = "message", []
        for line in response.iter_lines():
            if line == "":
                if data_lines:
                    yield event, json.loads("\n".join(data_lines))
                event, data_lines = "message", []
            elif line.startswith("event:"):
                event = line[6:].strip()
            elif line.startswith("data:"):
                data_lines.append(line[5:].lstrip())


    base = os.environ["ARCHY_API_URL"]
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ARCHY_TOKEN']}"}
    url = f"{base}/api/v1/orgs/{os.environ['ORG_ID']}/projects/{os.environ['PROJECT_ID']}/agents/{os.environ['AGENT_ID']}/chat/stream"

    with httpx.stream("POST", url, headers=headers, json={"message": "Hello"}, timeout=None) as response:
        response.raise_for_status()
        for event, data in sse_events(response):
            if event == "delta":
                print(data["delta"], end="", flush=True)
            elif event == "error":
                raise RuntimeError(data["detail"])
    ```

=== "TypeScript"

    ```typescript
    export async function* sse(response: Response): AsyncGenerator<{ event: string; data: any }> {
      const reader = response.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
      let buffer = "";
      for (;;) {
        const { value, done } = await reader.read();
        if (done) return;
        buffer += value;
        let boundary: number;
        while ((boundary = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
          const block = buffer.slice(0, boundary);
          buffer = buffer.slice(boundary + 2);
          let event = "message";
          const data: string[] = [];
          for (const line of block.split("\n")) {
            if (line.startsWith("event:")) event = line.slice(6).trim();
            else if (line.startsWith("data:")) data.push(line.slice(5).trimStart());
          }
          if (data.length) yield { event, data: JSON.parse(data.join("\n")) };
        }
      }
    }

    const response = await fetch(`${base}/api/v1/orgs/${org}/projects/${project}/agents/${agent}/chat/stream`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ message: "Hello" }),
    });
    for await (const { event, data } of sse(response)) {
      if (event === "delta") process.stdout.write(data.delta);
    }
    ```

### NDJSON: knowledge base retrieval preview

`POST .../agents/{agent_id}/query` with `{"kb_id": "...", "query": "...", "top_k": 3, "min_score": 0.2}` returns `application/x-ndjson`: one JSON object per line with an `event` field: `agent_start`, `retrieval` (the retrieved chunks), `agent_final` (its `response` joins the chunks) or `error` (with a `message`). It is a retrieval preview: no model is called.

```python
with httpx.stream("POST", url, headers=headers, json={"kb_id": kb_id, "query": "Refund window?"}, timeout=None) as r:
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line:
            event = json.loads(line)
            print(event)
```

## Workflow execution

### Synchronous

`POST .../workflows/{id}/execute` returns when the run finishes. See [Workflows](workflows.md#run-a-workflow) for the response. Use a generous client timeout: runs can take minutes.

### Streaming

`POST .../workflows/{id}/execute/stream` accepts the same body as `execute`.

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `start` | `{"workflow_id", "workflow_type", "session_id", "run_id"}` |
| `step_started`, `step_completed` | Per agent (orchestrator workflows) |
| `token`, `discussion` | Text from agents (other types) |
| `run.started`, `node.started`, `node.delta`, `node.completed`, `edge.active`, `run.completed` | The unified trace envelope: `{"v", "seq", "ts", "run_id", "workflow_id", ...}` |
| `structured_output` | The complete, validated object, sent once when a `structured_output_schema` is set; `run.completed` carries the same object |
| `end` | `{"session_id", "output", "structured_output", "audit", "error", "structured_output_error", "run_id", "status", "pending_input"}`. `status` is `awaiting_input` when the run paused at a checkpoint. |
| `error` | Replaces `end` on failure |

Treat unknown fields and event types as forward compatible. Each trace envelope has a `seq`.

!!! warning "A stream cannot reattach to a run in progress"
    Calling the endpoint again with a `session_id` and `?after_seq=<last seq>` first replays the persisted trace envelopes of that session with a higher `seq` (they are written when a run ends), and then starts a **new** run of the workflow with your `message` on that session. It does not attach to a run that is still executing, and `seq` restarts at 1 for each execution. For runs that must survive a disconnect, use [asynchronous runs](#asynchronous-runs).

```python
url = f"{base}/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/workflows/{workflow_id}/execute/stream"
body = {"message": "Run the weekly report", "inputs": {"week": "2026-W46"}}
with httpx.stream("POST", url, headers=headers, json=body, timeout=None) as r:
    for event, data in sse_events(r):
        if event == "node.started":
            print("running", data.get("node_id"))
        elif event == "end":
            print(data["status"], data["output"])
```

### Asynchronous runs

For callers that cannot stream, start a run and poll it.

```bash
# 1. Start. Same body as /execute. Returns immediately.
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/runs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Run the weekly report", "inputs": {"week": "2026-W46"}}'
# {"run_id": "…", "status": "pending"}   (HTTP 202)

# 2. Poll
curl -s "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/runs/$RUN_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

`status` is `pending`, `running`, `awaiting_input`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled` (a run paused at a checkpoint that was cancelled). `output`, `structured_output`, `audit` and `error` are filled once the run is `succeeded` or `failed`.

```python
import time


def run_and_wait(client, scope: str, workflow_id: str, message: str, *, timeout: float = 600, **inputs) -> dict:
    started = client.post(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs", json={"message": message, "inputs": inputs or None})
    started.raise_for_status()
    run_id = started.json()["run_id"]

    delay, deadline = 1.0, time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        run = client.get(f"{scope}/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs/{run_id}").json()
        if run["status"] in ("succeeded", "failed", "awaiting_input", "cancelled"):
            return run
        time.sleep(delay)
        delay = min(delay * 1.5, 10)  # back off to a 10 second poll
    raise TimeoutError(f"run {run_id} still running")
```

There is no endpoint that lists asynchronous runs, so keep the `run_id` you receive. `GET .../workflows/{id}/sessions` lists sessions.

!!! note "Service-token runs"
    A run started with a service token and no acting-user identity has no initiating user. Storage nodes can then only use project and organization connections that have a root folder, not personal connections.

## Pause and resume at a checkpoint

When a composite workflow reaches a `checkpoint` node the response has `status: "awaiting_input"`, `output` is the rendered prompt and `pending_input` describes the question: `{status, question, node_id, node_name, iteration}`. This holds for `/execute`, `/resume` and the stream `end` event. An **asynchronous run** reports `status: "awaiting_input"` with the prompt in `output` and the run's `session_id`; read the structured question from the session (`GET .../workflows/{id}/sessions/{session_id}`, `state.pending_input`).

```bash
# Resume with the answer
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/sessions/$SESSION_ID/resume" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"answer": "Approved. Add the pricing table."}'

# Or cancel; the run is marked cancelled and cannot resume
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/sessions/$SESSION_ID/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

- `answer` is 1 to 32,768 characters.
- Declared `sensitive` inputs are not stored with the paused run; send them again in `inputs` on resume. Any other key returns `422` with `detail.code = WORKFLOW_INPUTS_INVALID` (`INPUT_UNKNOWN`), and a missing required sensitive input gives `INPUT_REQUIRED`. The run keeps waiting.
- Passing the `session_id` of a paused run to `/execute` also resumes it. Invalid inputs return `422` and the run stays resumable.
- Checkpoints expire after 7 days by default. Expiry is detected when a resume is tried: that call returns `409` and marks the run `failed`. Until then the session still shows `awaiting_input`.

The full walkthrough is in [Human approval checkpoint](../tutorials/human-approval.md).

## Dialog runs

Multi-agent dialogs have their own resource: `POST .../dialog-runs` creates one, `POST .../dialog-runs/{run_id}/execute` streams it as NDJSON, and `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` manage it. See the [Workflows reference](../reference/workflows.md).

## Choosing timeouts

| Layer | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Client read timeout for streams | `None` (disabled) with your own idle watchdog |
| Client timeout for sync `execute` | 5 minutes or more |
| Proxies and gateways | Disable response buffering for `text/event-stream` and raise idle timeouts |
| Polling interval | 1 s growing to 10 s |


<!-- source: guides/mcp-servers-for-agents.md -->
# External MCP servers and skills

Agents become more useful when they can act: search Jira, query a database, call your internal API. The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** is the standard way to expose such tools. In Archy you **register** an MCP server once and **attach** it to the agents that may use it.

!!! info "Two different MCP topics"
    This page is about MCP servers that **agents call** (tools for your agents). To let **an AI client call Archy** (Claude, Copilot, Cursor, ...), see [MCP](../mcp/index.md).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    REG[Registered MCP server] -->|attach| AG[Agent]
    AG -->|tool call| REG
    REG --> EXT[Your tool service]
    HC[Health scheduler] -->|checks| REG
    AG --> LOG[Tool invocation log]
```

All paths below start with `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}`.

```bash
BASE="$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/projects/$PROJECT_ID"
```

## Register a server

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/mcp-servers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "tickets",
    "transport": "http",
    "config": {
      "base_url": "https://mcp.example.com",
      "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <service key for that server>"}
    }
  }'
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Human readable name (not enforced unique). `required_mcp_servers` entries match a server by id or by name, ignoring case and punctuation. |
| `transport` | `http` (or `streamable-http`) for a remote server. `stdio` servers are created from an organization template (see below); `transport` is ignored for template instances. |
| `config` | For `http`: `base_url`, optional `path` (default `/mcp`), `headers` and `stateful`. `env` values apply only to stdio template instances; for template instances `config` is validated against the template's schema (422 on mismatch). |
| `template_id`, `instance_label` | Create an instance of an organization template |

**Secrets are write-only.** All `headers` and `env` values, keys with credential-like names (token, api_key, password, secret), template fields marked `x-sensitive` and credentials inside URLs are encrypted at rest and returned as `***REDACTED***` by every endpoint. To keep a secret, send the placeholder back unchanged. To change it, send the new value. If an update adds a new URL origin, or changes a non-secret entry in the same `headers` or `env` block, re-enter the secrets too. Values that start with `enc:v1:` are rejected (422), and saving a secret fails with 503 when the deployment has no encryption key.

Remote server URLs are validated against SSRF rules. URLs must use `https://`; plain `http://`, private and loopback addresses need an operator setting (`SSRF_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS`, `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` or `SSRF_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS`), and cloud metadata hosts are always blocked.

## Attach to an agent

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/mcp-servers/$SERVER_ID/attach" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/mcp-servers" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/mcp-servers/$SERVER_ID/detach" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

In a composite workflow you can attach a server to one node with a `satellite-mcp` resource node instead. See [Attach resources](composite-workflows.md#attach-resources).

## Control which tools run

| Where | How |
|---|---|
| Per workflow node | `toolAllowlist` on the `satellite-mcp` node (omit to allow all) |
| Per run | `mcp_enabled: false` turns MCP off; `mcp_tool_allowlist: ["jira_get_issue"]` registers only those tools (server side names, without the server prefix) |
| Required servers | `required_mcp_servers` on a `sequential` or `composite` workflow fails the run with `MCP_UNAVAILABLE` when a server is down, instead of silently skipping it |

Pass the per-run options in the body of `/execute`, `/execute/stream` or `/runs`. They are not stored.

## Health and observability

| Need | Request |
|---|---|
| Latest health of a server | `GET .../mcp-servers/{server_id}/health/latest` |
| History | `GET .../mcp-servers/{server_id}/health` |
| Check now (platform admins only; at most once per 30 seconds per server, otherwise `429`) | `POST .../mcp-servers/{server_id}/health/check` |
| Status of an agent's servers | `GET .../agents/{agent_id}/mcp-status` |
| Tool invocation log | `GET .../mcp/tool-invocations` |
| One invocation | `GET .../mcp/tool-invocations/{invocation_id}` |
| Metrics of invocations | `GET .../mcp/tool-invocations/metrics` |
| Re-run an invocation (at most 10 per minute per project) | `POST .../mcp/tool-invocations/{invocation_id}/replay` |

A background scheduler checks each project's servers every 60 seconds by default (`GET {base_url}/health` for HTTP servers) and backs off up to 300 seconds after failures. The interval cannot be changed through the API; operators can turn the scheduler off with `HEALTH_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false`.

## Organization templates

Platform administrators publish **templates** that describe how to reach or launch a server and which config fields are sensitive. Projects then create **instances** from a template with their own values. Templates are the only way to run `stdio` servers: creating a stdio server without a template returns `403`, and the command always comes from the template and must be an approved command (default `npx`, `uvx`, `uv`, `node`, `python`, `python3`). An instance can only set the env keys its template declares.

```bash
# List the templates of the organization
curl -s "$ARCHY_API_URL/api/v1/orgs/$ORG_ID/mcp-templates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Create an instance from a template
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/mcp-servers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"name\": \"jira-prod\", \"transport\": \"stdio\", \"template_id\": \"$TEMPLATE_ID\", \"instance_label\": \"production\", \"config\": {}}"
```

## Skills

A **skill** is an instruction set (a `SKILL.md` document) that is appended to the system prompt on every run of an agent it is enabled or attached on. There are two kinds.

- **Skills on disk**: shipped with the deployment. `GET /api/v1/skills` lists them, `GET /api/v1/skills/{skill_id}` shows metadata and `GET /api/v1/skills/{skill_id}/content` returns the `SKILL.md`. Enable them on an agent with `config.skills_enabled`.
- **Skills in the database**: created through the API and scoped to a project.

```bash
# Create a skill
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/skills" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "refund-policy", "description": "How to handle refund requests", "skill_content": "# Refund policy\n\nRefunds are allowed within 30 days..."}'

# Attach it to an agent
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/skills" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"skill_id\": \"$SKILL_ID\"}"

# List, detach
curl -s "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/skills" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/agents/$AGENT_ID/skills/$SKILL_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

## Atlassian access for agents

An agent can use Jira and Confluence on behalf of a person. The person creates a personal **Atlassian connection** (`POST /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/integrations/atlassian`), then **grants** it to an agent (`PUT .../agents/{agent_id}/integration-grants`). The credentials never leave the platform and the agent acts only while that person initiates the run. See the [Connections and integrations reference](../reference/connections.md).


<!-- source: guides/sessions-artifacts-usage.md -->
# Sessions, artifacts and usage

## Sessions

A **session** is the persisted record of a conversation with an agent or a run of a workflow: messages, tool calls, retrievals, errors and the per-node trace of workflow runs.

All paths start with `/api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}`.

| Action | Request |
|---|---|
| List sessions (agent and workflow) | `GET .../sessions?limit=50&offset=0` |
| Read one with its history | `GET .../sessions/{session_id}` |
| Activity events (tool calls, retrievals, errors) | `GET .../sessions/{session_id}/activity` |
| Files created during the session | `GET .../sessions/{session_id}/artifacts` |
| Rename | `PATCH .../sessions/{session_id}/rename` |
| Generate a name from the content | `POST .../sessions/{session_id}/regenerate-name` |
| Delete | `DELETE .../sessions/{session_id}` |
| Sessions that involved an agent | `GET /api/v1/agents/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/agents/{agent_id}/sessions` |
| Workflow sessions | `GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/sessions` (optional `status` filter) |
| One workflow session with its trace | `GET .../workflows/{workflow_id}/sessions/{session_id}` |

```bash
curl -s "$BASE/sessions?limit=20" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

```json
[
  {
    "session_id": "4e7c87f4-30d4-565f-a47b-9b4fca7f385a",
    "created_at": "2026-11-17T09:09:03",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-17T09:12:44",
    "name": "Refund policy question",
    "last_agent_id": "26fc2a0e-afe5-4c01-849b-eac03777464e"
  }
]
```

Workflow sessions expose a status: `completed`, `awaiting_input` (paused at a checkpoint), `failed` (a checkpoint failed, for example expired) or `cancelled`. Note that `completed` only means "no waiting, failed or cancelled marker".

!!! tip "Build an audit view"
    Combine `GET .../sessions/{id}` (messages), `.../activity` (tool calls and retrievals) and, for workflows, the session trace to show users exactly what an agent did and why.

## Artifacts

An **artifact** is a file stored with a project: the output of a `save-file` or `storage-read` node, an export of a run, or an upload.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RUN[Workflow run] -->|save-file node| ART[(Artifact)]
    RUN -->|export run output| ART
    UP[Your upload] --> ART
    ART --> DL[Download]
    ART --> NODE[Later node: nodes.x.files]
```

### Upload

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/artifacts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN" \
  -F "file=@report.pdf" -F "name=weekly-report.pdf" -F "media_type=application/pdf"
```

Optional form fields link the file to its origin: `run_id`, `session_id`, `node_id` (up to 255 characters) and `agent_id`.

### List, read, download, delete

```bash
# Filter by run, node, session, media type or source
curl -s "$BASE/artifacts?run_id=$RUN_ID&limit=50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Metadata: name, media type, size, sha256, source, expiry
curl -s "$BASE/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Download (always served as an attachment)
curl -s -o report.pdf "$BASE/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID/download" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"

# Delete (soft delete; the stored blob is removed within 24 hours)
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/artifacts/$ARTIFACT_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

### Export a run's output as a file

After a run finishes, turn its final output (or one node's output) into a file:

`POST .../workflows/{workflow_id}/runs/{run_id}/exports`

The response is the new artifact. Supported formats include `markdown`, `text`, `json`, `html`, `csv`, `docx` and `xlsx`.

### Limits

Defaults are set by the operator and can differ per deployment.

| Limit | Default |
|---|---|
| File size | 25 MB |
| Files per run | 100 |
| Storage per project | 1 GB |
| Storage per organization | 2 GB |
| Retention | 90 days |

Exceeding a limit returns an error naming the limit.

## Token usage

Every model call records its token usage. Query it at project or organization level.

| Question | Project endpoint | Organization endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| Totals grouped by something | `GET .../token-usage/aggregations` | `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/aggregations` |
| Per model | `GET .../token-usage/metrics/by-model` | `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/metrics/by-model` |
| Over time | `GET .../token-usage/metrics/timeseries` | `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/metrics/timeseries` |
| Chart ready data | `GET .../token-usage/charts` | `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/token-usage/charts` |
| Individual events | `GET .../token-usage/events` | |

```bash
curl -s "$BASE/token-usage/aggregations?group_by=model&token_type=total" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARCHY_TOKEN"
```

```json
{"group_by": "model", "token_type": "total", "items": []}
```

Query parameters of `aggregations`:

| Parameter | Values |
|---|---|
| `group_by` | `model`, `provider`, `agent`, `workflow`, `project`, `day`, `week`, `month` |
| `token_type` | `input`, `output`, `total` |
| `since`, `until` | Time window |
| `model`, `models`, `agent_id`, `workflow_id`, `session_id` | Filters |
| `period` | `last_7d`, `last_30d` or `last_90d` |
| `order_by`, `order_dir` | `tokens`, `calls` or `group`; `asc` or `desc` |
| `min_tokens`, `max_tokens`, `limit`, `offset` | Thresholds and paging (`limit` 1 to 200) |

The timeseries endpoint takes `granularity` of `day` or `hour` and returns buckets with `call_count`, `prompt_tokens` and completion tokens.
